jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer - Databases Tempo | Canada | Remote
jobs.excerpt: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale.
jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position. We are seeking candidates in US and Canada.

The Opportunity:

We build Tempo, the open-source distributed tracing backend behind Grafana Cloud Traces and Grafana Enterprise Traces (GET). Tempo makes it easy to search traces, generate metrics from spans, and connect tracing data with logs, metrics, and profiles across the Grafana stack.

2026 is an inflection point for Tempo. After a major architectural upgrade and the launch of TraceQL metrics, we are shifting from foundational work to product and operational excellence, and evolving Tempo from a SaaS database into a platform that powers Grafana’s next generation of observability products (App Observability, Asserts, Traces Drilldown, and AI-driven assistants).

Over the next year, you will help us:

  • Make Grafana Cloud Traces “just work” for customers by eliminating rough edges, confusing limits, and hidden failure modes.
  • Achieve operational excellence at scale as we grow from close to 50 cells today into triple digits this year, with autoscaling, parameterized rollouts, and aggressive toil reduction.
  • Evolve Tempo into a platform enabler: higher-density APIs, trace aggregation, TraceQL metrics math, and machine/LLM-friendly interfaces that downstream products and agents can build on.
  • Push performance further: faster query latency at hundreds of MB/s ingestion and performant 30-day query ranges to match competitors.
  • Prepare Tempo for an agent-driven world: larger, burstier, higher-cardinality workloads, and new categories of AI-powered workflows, such as assistant-driven triage and “why is this slow?”- style investigations.

What You’ll Be Doing:

As a Senior Engineer on Tempo, you will own technical direction on the hardest problems in our roadmap and raise the bar across the team.

  • Deliver significant technical projects. Take well-scoped, multi-month initiatives from problem framing through rollout, e.g., trace aggregation APIs, Limitless Tempo, autoscaling cells and customer limits, or query engine improvements. Partner with Staff engineers and the tech lead on broader, cross-team direction.
  • Own major components of Tempo. Contribute to and own parts of ingestion, storage, query, and metrics generation. Write and present design docs, participate in design reviews, make sound trade-offs on performance, cost, and complexity, and document the “why” for the team.
  • Build APIs for humans and agents. Help shape the next generation of Tempo’s interfaces (structured, deterministic, discoverable) so that Act 3 products, LLM-driven assistants, and external integrators can build on Tempo reliably.
  • Contribute to operational excellence. Own outcomes for the areas you build against concrete SLOs (P99 write latency, incident recurrence, TCO per ingested GB), and help move the team toward Zero Ops through automation, parameterized rollouts, and actionable alerts.
  • Collaborate with Product and sibling teams. Work with PMs and with App Observability, Asserts, Drilldown, and Grafana Assistant teams to understand how Tempo gets consumed and to ship what unblocks them.
  • Mentor and support engineers. Raise the bar through thorough code review, constructive design feedback, and pairing, especially with junior and mid-level engineers.
  • Participate in on-call for the services you help build, and contribute to incident response and post-incident learning.
  • Contribute to open source. Tempo is OSS. You will engage the community, review external contributions, and contribute to the project in the open.

We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction. We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups—always with strong code review and quality standards. You'll also have access to the latest frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

Example problems you could work on

These are the kinds of projects landing in 2026:

  • Trace aggregation and higher-density APIs: extend TraceQL metrics, design LLM-friendly response types, and make Tempo a first-class data source for Grafana’s AI assistant.
  • Autoscaling end-to-end: customer limits and Tempo cells, with hysteresis, predictive scaling for spikes, and safe scale-down.
  • Agent-scale ingestion and query: guardrails for bursty, high-cardinality, agent-generated workloads.
  • Query performance: new data formats, smarter query pipelines, targeted optimizations for common Drilldown and Traces workflows, and 30-day query ranges.
  • Rollouts and multi-cell operations: parameterized rollouts, push-button deploys, and the tooling to grow safely into triple-digit cell counts without a proportional increase in alert noise.
  • Limits and self-service: drive customer-facing configuration and observability so escalations trend toward zero.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

  • Technical ownership. A track record of delivering complex, multi-month projects that spanned design, delivery, and operations, and of helping the teammates around you grow.
  • Solid systems experience. Significant hands-on experience building and operating distributed data systems in production: ingestion pipelines, storage engines, query execution, or similar.
  • Strong software craftsmanship. You write clean, robust, performant software that others can maintain, and you know when to optimize vs. when to ship.
  • Strong Go, or a path to it. We write Tempo in Go. Solid experience in other systems languages (Rust, C, C++) translates well.
  • Operational mindset. You’ve owned production services, carried a pager, reduced toil, and treated SLOs as a product feature, not a chore.
  • Customer focus and pragmatism. You break complex problems into short feedback loops: analyze, design, deliver an MVP, learn, iterate.
  • Collaboration and clear writing. You contribute through design docs, reviews, and shipped code, and you communicate clearly in a fully remote, asynchronous environment.

Bonus Points For:

  • Experience with tracing, OpenTelemetry, or large-scale observability systems.
  • Experience designing query languages, SQL/TraceQL-like engines, or APIs intended to be consumed programmatically (by services or agents).
  • Experience with columnar storage formats (e.g., Parquet) or purpose-built on-disk formats for analytical workloads.
  • Experience operating multi-tenant, multi-cell SaaS infrastructure at scale on Kubernetes.
  • Experience building for AI/LLM consumers: structured APIs, metadata/discovery endpoints, deterministic outputs, evaluation harnesses.
  • Open-source contribution or maintainership, and comfort engaging a community in the open.
  • Experience as an on-call user of Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, or Tempo in a previous role (or on a homelab).
  • Experience in a fully remote, globally distributed team.

How we work

We are a remote-first team that meets regularly over video and does most of our work asynchronously, in writing. We value creativity, diverse perspectives, and clear communication. Tempo is relied upon by prominent global organizations to monitor critical applications and infrastructure, and we expect everyone on the team, including our senior engineers, to contribute ideas that make it a more reliable, more useful, and more loved product.

In Canada, the OTE (On-Target Earnings)/Base compensation range for this role is CAD $164,490 - $197,389. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
  • Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

Equal Opportunity Employer:Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow.

Grafana Labs may utilize AI tools in its recruitment process to assist in matching information provided in CVs to job postings. The recruitment team will continue to review inbound CVs manually to identify alignment with current openings.

For information about how your personal data is used once you’ve applied to a job, check out our privacy policy.

jobs.description:
About us

SwimOutlet is the largest online specialty retailer for swimming and water sports in the US, and part of Spiraledge, whose brands include EverydayYoga, Swim.com, Practyce and Tend.

About the Role

SwimOutlet is looking for a driven, relationship-focused Facility Sales Specialist to help grow our business with aquatic facilities and organizations. In this role you'll work with municipal and community pools, YMCAs, colleges and universities, K–12 schools, swim clubs, fitness centers, resorts, and other aquatic facilities. You’ll serve as their trusted partner for facility, deck and pool gear.

You'll be responsible for supporting the sales cycle: prospecting new facilities, supporting existing relationships, understanding each facility's operational and seasonal needs, and delivering solutions that keep their programs equipped year-round. Reporting to the VP of Sales and Service, you'll be a key contributor to the growth of SwimOutlet's facility and B2B business.

What You'll Do

  • Support and grow facility sales, driving revenue against monthly, quarterly, and annual targets.
  • Prospect and qualify new facility opportunities through outbound outreach, referrals, industry events, and inbound leads.
  • Build long-term relationships with aquatics directors, facility managers, coaches, purchasing agents, and other decision-makers.
  • Consult with facilities to understand their programming, headcount, seasonal cycles, and budgets, then recommend the right product mix.
  • Prepare quotes, proposals, and bulk/team orders; manage pricing within approved guidelines.
  • Coordinate with customer service, operations, and fulfillment to ensure accurate, on-time delivery and a smooth account experience.
  • Log sales activity and customer interactions in the CRM, keeping records current.
  • Handle contract renewals, reorders, and account issues, resolving problems quickly to protect and grow the relationship.
  • Stay current on product lines, new arrivals, and category trends to advise customers credibly.
  • Partner with marketing and leadership on facility-focused promotions and initiatives.
  • Represent SwimOutlet at trade shows, aquatic conferences, and regional events as needed.

Who you are

  • Experience selling to aquatic facilities, athletic departments, schools, or in sporting goods / team dealer channels.
  • Familiarity with the aquatics, swim, or fitness industry (personal involvement in swimming a plus).
  • Experience with team/bulk ordering, custom apparel, or facility supply programs.
  • Willingness to travel within territory and attend industry events.
  • 2+ years of B2B sales, account management, or inside/outside sales experience, ideally with a track record of hitting quota.
  • Strong relationship-building, consultative selling, and negotiation skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; comfortable presenting to and following up with decision-makers.
  • Organized and self-directed, able to prioritize across many facility leads and requests.
  • Proficiency with CRM tools (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot) and standard sales/productivity software.

About the Job:

Sanofi focuses on developing specialty treatments for debilitating diseases that are often difficult to diagnose and treat, providing hope to patients and their families.

Sanofi has pioneered the development and delivery of transformative therapies for patients affected by rare and debilitating diseases for over 30 years. We accomplish our goals through world-class research, collaboration with the global patient community, and with the compassion and commitment of our employees. With a focus on rare diseases, oncology, immunology, and multiple sclerosis, we are dedicated to making a positive impact on the lives of the patients and families we serve. Sanofi's portfolio of transformative therapies, which are marketed in countries around the world, represent groundbreaking and life-saving advances in medicine.

At Sanofi, we are committed to the growth of our people, connected in purpose by career, life, and health. Learn more at .

The Rare Blood Disorders franchise is a patient-centric organization responsible for delivering the highest quality education and service regarding disease and treatment. The goal of the franchise is to penetrate existing and new markets to meet business goals by educating physicians and healthcare professionals on a portfolio of products while upholding the Company's mission and values.


Sanofi's Rare Blood Disorders/Rare Hematology Thought Leader Liaison (TLL) is a field-based, commercial role responsible for engaging Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) and Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) to strategically inform market development across the rare hematology portfolio of products. The TLL is expected to possess a high level of clinical and customer knowledge, have experience with both field and headquarters protocols and procedures, and possess the drive and spirit to engage with healthcare professionals to help build educational platforms, generate insights, and inform local and national brand strategies, supporting the commercial success of the portfolio. The portfolio focus is primarily on Systemic Mastocytosis (SM) and Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP).

The TLL will work closely, and within approved SOPs, with other field professionals including, but not limited to, Regional Business Directors, Area Business Managers, and Medical Science Liaisons, as well as home office-based colleagues in Marketing, Medical Affairs, Operations, and Market Access.

A core responsibility of this role is driving SM and ITP market development within the assigned region — identifying KOLs and fostering multi-disciplinary connections across specialists who treat and manage SM and ITP patients. The TLL serves as a strategic partner to cross-functional commercial and medical teams. The TLL helps to shape brand strategy through insight generation, KOL engagement, and regional market development initiatives across the full rare hematology portfolio.

Join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological conditions. In Specialty Care, you'll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs.

About Sanofi:

We’re an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives.

Main Responsibilities:

*All TLL interactions are on-label and consistent with commercial compliance, legal, and regulatory guidelines.*

A. KOL Development and Engagement

  • Work with cross-functional colleagues to coordinate function-specific activities aligned to business and customer needs
  • Identify, profile, and maintain long-term partnerships with KOLs and emerging leaders within the Hematology and Allergy/Immunology communities

  • Engage in on-label conversations to gather insights on topics such as disease diagnosis and treatment, therapeutic options, and product positioning across SM and ITP.
  • Execute unique, on-label, and strategic HCP programming (e.g., disease state and product) as determined by brand needs
  • Serve as a single point of contact to resolve commercial KOL issues
  • Execute a customer-centric, needs-based approach with targeted KOLs
  • Plan and execute KOL engagements and executive encounters at local, regional, and national conferences, field visits, and other venues as directed
  • Be a voice for allergy/immunology and hematology/oncology KOLs within the organization, sharing insights with key stakeholders and cross-functional partners to inform brand strategy

B. SM and ITP Centers of Excellence and Market Development

  • Lead long-term market development efforts in assigned regions across the SM and ITP landscapes, focusing on high-potential centers and customers
  • Develop and execute customer engagement plans for KOLs within assigned regions, accountable for fostering KOL connections across multi-disciplinary specialists who treat and manage SM and ITP patients
  • Maintain understanding of regional market dynamics, including key opinion leaders, institutional accounts, and multi-disciplinary teams to advance SM and ITP patient care and partner with sales leadership and commercial field teams to align regional market development strategies
  • Develop and execute regional marketing initiatives (insight discovery, advisory boards, roundtables, etc.)
  • Support regional congress planning and execution, including KOL insight gathering engagement at priority conferences across hematology/oncology and allergy/immunology, in partnership with Medical, Sales Leadership, Commercial Operations, and Brand Marketing
  • Proactively meet with assigned centers and/or customers to solicit feedback and adjust strategies accordingly
  • Develop and continuously maintain a high level of clinical competence across SM, ITP, and aTTP

C. Market Insights and Collaboration

  • Capture, analyze, and share customer insights aligned with brand priorities across SM and ITP.
  • Work with targeted KOLs to obtain feedback on new and existing brand-related strategies and materials (all materials and programs will be approved by legal, compliance, and regulatory)
  • Capture and analyze competitive intelligence to help shape strategy and activities
  • Facilitate cross-functional planning, recruitment, and execution of regional and national advisory boards in partnership with HQ Marketing.
  • Identify, align, and recruit appropriate HCP/KOL consultants to meet the needs of marketing and achieve aligned KPIs for each project
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to inform account strategy and plans through treatment pathway discovery and insight generation to advance care in centers of excellence

D. Speaker Bureau Operations and Content

  • Assist with speaker bureau management, including identification and training/coaching of promotional speakers with approved slide decks and materials
  • Assist in the execution of speaker contracting when requested, including completion of annual budget plans, recommendations, and nominations
  • Coordinate and execute speaker training to ensure assigned speakers are competent, compliant, and up to date on new information
  • Attend HCP speaker programs to observe, coach, and remediate speakers when necessary to ensure optimal execution of content
  • Assist with new content creation and existing content updates and renewals
  • Serve as the single point of contact for a high-volume of speaker logistics/scheduling and work cross-functionally to ensure streamlined communication
  • Lead planning, execution, and pull-through of TLL-owned programs

About You:

Key Capabilities:

  • Strong communication, organization, and project management skills
  • Proven ability to work in a highly dynamic and fast-paced environment
  • Demonstrated ability to lead without formal authority and work in a highly collaborative environment
  • Excellent organizational, interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills
  • Passionate, confident, articulate, and comfortable in a team environment
  • Ability to successfully engage with top KOLs and other HCPs
  • Expertise in creating and executing customer account plans
  • Robust analytical and problem-solving skills; ability to identify and act on creative solutions
  • Ability to establish credibility, connect the dots, and align multiple stakeholders to pioneer the adoption of new products, methods, and technologies
  • Flexibility and ability to plan and adapt to changing market conditions
  • Motivated by patient focus, urgency, and personal commitment to high performance, results, and compliance
  • Possesses high integrity and exceptional work ethic

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree

Preferred Qualifications:

jobs.excerpt: For decades, DTN has been the silent force behind some of the world’s most critical industries—helping businesses navigate complexity, uncertainty, and risk with smarter, faster decisions.
jobs.description:
For decades, DTN has been the silent force behind some of the world’s most critical industries—helping businesses navigate complexity, uncertainty, and risk with smarter, faster decisions. From agriculture to energy to weather intelligence, our proprietary Operational Decisioning Platform transforms raw data into decision-grade insights—enabling companies to optimize supply chains, ensure market stability, and safeguard infrastructure against disruption. We don’t follow trends—we set the standard for precision, trust, and operational impact.

DTN is at an exciting inflection point. Building off a foundation of financial strength, profitability, and industry trust, we’re accelerating growth and expanding our global footprint. Our purpose-built solutions—powered by AI and honed by decades of vertical expertise—are helping some of the world’s most significant enterprises thrive amid operational constraints and uncover new opportunities in a fast-changing world.

Job Description:


Position Summary:


DTN is seeking a high-energy, results-driven Account Executive – Agriculture to identify, prospect, and acquire new business opportunities within the agriculture industry.


This position is designed for a sales professional who thrives in a hunter-oriented environment, with a strong focus on lead generation, strategic prospecting, building qualified pipelines, and securing new customers. You will leverage your industry knowledge, professional network, and consultative selling skills to identify customer needs, position DTN's solutions, and demonstrate measurable business value.


As an Account Executive, you will own the new customer acquisition process, from identifying opportunities and engaging decision-makers through negotiating and closing business. Following a successful sale, you will transition new customers to the Account Management team for ongoing relationship management, while ensuring a seamless customer experience.


The ideal candidate is self-motivated, adaptable, commercially driven, and confident engaging with executive-level stakeholders. You will bring a strong understanding of the agriculture sector, SaaS and software sales experience, and the ability to communicate compelling industry insights that differentiate DTN in the marketplace.


What You Will Be Responsible For:


Prospecting and Lead Generation

  • Identify and pursue new business opportunities and prospective customers that align with DTN's agriculture solutions and commercial objectives.

  • Leverage existing industry relationships, professional networks, and referrals to conduct warm outreach and generate qualified leads.
  • Execute proactive prospecting activities through cold calling, email outreach, professional networking, trade shows, and other business development channels.
  • Build and maintain a strong pipeline of qualified prospects through market research, strategic account targeting, and consistent lead generation activities.
  • Stay informed on agriculture industry trends, competitive activity, evolving market conditions, and customer business needs to identify and pursue new opportunities.

Sales and New Customer Acquisition

  • Engage C-suite executives and other senior decision-makers with a consultative approach, providing relevant industry perspectives, business insights, and strategic recommendations.
  • Develop and deliver compelling sales presentations and proposals that demonstrate DTN's capabilities and align solutions with customer business priorities.
  • Position DTN's products and services as solutions to customer challenges, communicating differentiated value and relevant business outcomes.
  • Leverage internal DTN expertise, resources, and product knowledge to identify and present cross-selling opportunities to prospective customers when appropriate.
  • Partner with Marketing to develop and execute targeted campaigns designed to attract high-potential prospects and generate new business opportunities.
  • Lead commercial discussions and negotiate pricing, contract terms, and business agreements to successfully secure new customer relationships.
  • Consistently meet or exceed monthly and quarterly sales targets focused on new customer acquisition.
  • Maintain a consultative, professional, and adaptable sales approach, adjusting messaging and strategy in response to customer needs, business discussions, and changing circumstances.

Account Transition and Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Ensure a smooth and effective transition of newly acquired customers to the Account Management team for ongoing relationship management.
  • Provide detailed customer insights, business requirements, expectations, and relevant sales history to support a successful account handoff.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Operations, Finance, Marketing, and Account Management to support customer success and business growth.
  • Maintain accurate prospect information, sales activities, and pipeline updates within Salesforce to support effective sales execution and visibility.

What You Will Bring to the Position:


  • 4+ years of experience in B2B sales, new business development, or customer acquisition.
  • 4+ years of experience in SaaS and software sales.
  • Strong understanding of the agriculture industry and its business environment.
  • Proven ability to identify and pursue new prospects, engage qualified leads, develop business opportunities, and successfully close deals.
  • Demonstrated success in a hunter-oriented sales environment focused on acquiring new customers.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, and professional networking skills.
  • Ability to engage senior business leaders and C-suite executives with relevant industry insights and a consultative sales approach.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce (SFDC) for lead tracking, pipeline management, and sales activity documentation.
  • Strong customer-facing skills and a professional, consultative approach to understanding and addressing business needs.
  • Ability to think quickly, adapt sales conversations in real time, and pivot from prepared messaging based on customer feedback and discussion.
  • Ability to adapt effectively to changing market conditions, customer requirements, and business priorities.
  • Self-motivation, initiative, a results-driven mindset, and a strong passion for sales growth and new business development.

What Will Make You Stand Out:


  • Established professional relationships and networks within the agriculture industry that can support new business development.
  • Experience selling SaaS, software, data, analytics, or technology solutions to agriculture-related businesses.
  • Demonstrated success selling to senior executives and translating industry insights into compelling commercial opportunities.
  • Experience developing new territories, prospecting into untapped accounts, or building a qualified sales pipeline from the ground up.
  • Ability to identify opportunities to introduce multiple solutions across a prospective customer's business.
  • Experience collaborating with Marketing and cross-functional commercial teams to accelerate lead generation and new customer acquisition.

What You Can Expect from DTN:


  • Competitive Salary
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Flexible working hours
  • Remote work model (position dependent)
  • Competitive Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance Plans
  • 6% 401K matching
  • Unlimited access to 13k+ courses via learning platform to support employee career advancement
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Compensation:

The targeted hiring base pay range for this position is between $82,000 and $108,000. DTN is a pay for performance organization, which means there is the opportunity to advance your compensation with performance over time. The actual base pay offered for this position will be dependent upon many factors, including but not limited to: prior work experience, training/education, transferable skills, business needs, internal equity and applicable laws. The targeted hiring base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role may also be eligible for market competitive variable pay and benefits.


About DTN:

DTN is a global data and technology company helping operational leaders in energy, agriculture, and weather-driven industries make faster, smarter decisions. Our Operational Decisioning Platform turns complex data into decision-grade insights—empowering customers to expand their margins, accelerate growth, and outpace risk. With more than 1,200 employees globally, DTN serves the companies that feed, fuel, and protect the world.

At DTN, we value clarity,trust, and action. We’re a team of problem-solvers, outcome-drivers, and industry nerds who believe that precision matters – and that mission is at the core of what we do.

  • Trust Built: We earn it. We keep it. We protect it. Our neutrality, precision, and integrity are non-negotiable.

  • Confidence-Driven: We help customers move with clarity and conviction. We bring the data and operational knowledge leaders need to act.

  • Built for Industry: We speak operations because we come from operations. Our expertise is forged in fuel terminals, fields, flight paths, and forecasts.

  • Future-Forward: We see what’s coming- and we’re ready. We help customers lead through change with smarter decisioning.

Recruitment Fraud Notice:

DTN is aware of incidents where external parties have impersonated our organization, issuing fraudulent communications and/or job offers. Please be advised that all legitimate communication from DTN will come from an official @dtn.com email address. Any offers are extended directly by our Talent Acquisition team following a formal interview process.


If you receive a suspicious message or offer claiming to be from DTN, please do not engage. Contact our Talent Acquisition team at to verify the legitimacy of any communication. Report any fraudulent messaging as phishing or spam.

About This Opportunity

Purple Squirrel Enterprises has been supporting startups and global firms through growth, change, and expansion for 19+ years. We provide flexible HR and recruiting solutions that allow leaders to focus on strategy while we handle people operations — and this search is no exception.

We are exclusively engaged by a high-growth health technology company to help them identify and hire exceptional talent for this role. Applications submitted directly to our client will be redirected back to Purple Squirrel Enterprises. To be considered for this role, all candidates must apply through this posting.

About Our Client

Our client was founded on a mission to transform medication management for vulnerable populations through innovation, accountability, and compassion. Their platform empowers care teams by simplifying complex workflows, preventing medication errors, and ensuring compliance — ultimately improving safety, outcomes, and independence for individuals in long-term care and other specialized care settings.

They operate like a family: supporting one another both professionally and personally, listening first, building with empathy, and remaining committed to solving problems that have a meaningful, real-world impact on people's lives.

💜 This company was built around a cause that is both personal and urgent. That authenticity shows in how they operate, who they hire, and what they build. If you are looking for work that matters — this is it.

About the Role

As part of the Customer Experience team, the Enterprise Customer Success Manager – State Lead will serve as the strategic leader for the company's medication management customer success programming across Louisiana. This role is responsible for ensuring successful implementation, adoption, and expansion of the platform across participating providers throughout the state.

The Enterprise CSM will own executive relationships with program stakeholders and partner organizations while leading and mentoring a team of In-State Customer Success Managers responsible for provider engagement and frontline program support. This role requires strong leadership, program management, and the ability to drive measurable outcomes across complex healthcare and government environments.

What You'll Do

Enterprise Program Leadership
  • Serve as the primary strategic owner of programming within the state, ensuring program success across participating providers
  • Manage relationships with stakeholders across multiple levels — agency leadership, executive sponsors, program administrators, provider executives, and clinical leaders
  • Own full-stack customer success support across software, hardware, and services for the enterprise program

    • Program planning and coordination
    • Cross-functional collaboration with Product, Engineering, and Operations
    • Platform configuration and readiness
    • Quality assurance (QA)
    • Go-live execution and post-implementation optimization
  • Drive enterprise adoption and outcomes across the provider network
  • Deliver executive-level communications including Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), performance reporting, and program updates
  • Partner closely with Product and Engineering to represent enterprise customer needs, capture feedback, and influence roadmap priorities
  • Ensure strong program performance across key success metrics including adoption, program health, satisfaction, and measurable ROI
Team Leadership & People Management
  • Lead and manage a team of 1–3 In-State Customer Success Managers supporting providers across the state
  • Serve as the first point of escalation for customer issues and help resolve complex provider challenges
  • Partner with leadership on recruiting and hiring activities, including job description development, interview planning, and candidate evaluation
  • Onboard and train new In-State Customer Success Managers, maintaining and improving onboarding guides and enablement materials
  • Support the growth and development of team members through regular 1:1s, performance reviews, individual development plans, and coaching
  • Contribute to building a scalable Customer Experience organization capable of supporting continued enterprise and government program growth
Strategic Growth & Program Development
  • Act as the internal program leader for providers in the state, ensuring alignment between customer needs and company strategic goals
  • Identify and implement operational improvements that scale the customer experience as enterprise programs expand
  • Lead and support upsells and expansion opportunities within the enterprise program
  • Document customer insights, feature requests, and program feedback to inform product development and roadmap planning
  • Represent Customer Success in cross-functional initiatives and executive-level strategic discussions
How We Measure Success
KPIDescriptionNet Revenue Retention (NRR)Retention and expansion of account revenueRenewal RateOn-time renewal of program contractsUpsell & Expansion RevenueNew revenue generated within the enterprise programNet Promoter Score (NPS)Program stakeholder satisfactionCustomer Satisfaction (CSAT)Satisfaction ratings across the provider networkCustomer Health ScoreOngoing account/program health trackingEnterprise Implementation & Go-Live SuccessOn-time, high-quality rolloutsAdoption Across Participating ProvidersPlatform utilization across the state
What Success Looks Like
  • Deep Partnership: You have developed a meaningful, trusting relationship with program stakeholders. They view the company not just as a vendor, but as a critical strategic partner in their mission to improve resident safety and program accountability.
  • Operational Harmony: The "State Model" for software deployment is seen as a gold standard within the company — high adoption rates, minimal deployment friction, measurable ROI for providers.
  • Team Excellence: You have built a high-performing In-State CSM team that feels supported, coached, and empowered to navigate the unique challenges of frontline healthcare environments.
  • Program Expansion: Your leadership has secured the program's longevity through high renewal rates and identification of new opportunities to expand impact within the state's healthcare ecosystem.
What We're Looking For

Required
  • 7+ years of experience in Customer Success, Enterprise Account Management, or a similar customer-facing role — preferably within healthcare SaaS
  • Demonstrated success managing large enterprise or government accounts with complex stakeholder environments
  • Direct people management experience — leading, hiring, onboarding, and developing customer success or account management teams
  • Strong program and project management skills with experience delivering multi-site implementations
  • Excellent communication skills with executive presence and experience engaging C-suite and public sector stakeholders
  • Ability to balance strategic program leadership with tactical execution
  • Experience with customer success tools and platforms (e.g., HubSpot, JIRA, Confluence, or similar)
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time
  • Must reside in Louisiana
Preferred
  • Healthcare industry knowledge including HIPAA, DEA compliance, and electronic medical records (Epic, Cerner, Meditech, etc.)
  • Experience with government or public-sector program administration

Compensation & Benefits

Our client offers a competitive, comprehensive package designed to support your well-being and long-term growth:
  • $95,000 – $118,000 base salary + variable compensation plan (commensurate with experience)
  • 100% company-paid medical coverage (base plan)
  • Dental & vision available
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Company-paid life, AD&D, STD & LTD insurance
  • Lifestyle Spending Account (wellness, personal use, and company swag)
  • Flexible PTO + company holidays
  • Flexible, remote-friendly work environment
  • 💜 Mission-driven work with real impact on vulnerable populations

Why This Role — And Why Now
  • Real problems, real stakes — your work will directly support organizations delivering care to vulnerable populations
  • High-growth trajectory — significant state and program expansion already underway
  • True strategic ownership — you will own an entire state's program, not a slice of a larger portfolio
  • High-trust, collaborative culture — small team, strong relationships, fast decisions, accessible leadership
  • Career growth — high visibility with leadership and real opportunity to grow as the company scales
  • 💜 Authentic mission — this company was built around a cause that matters, and that authenticity permeates everything they do
Working With Purple Squirrel Enterprises

We are exclusively engaged by this client — meaning we are not one of many agencies submitting resumes. We are their dedicated recruiting partner, embedded in their process, and we know this role inside and out.

Here's what that means for you as a candidate:

How You Will Do It

  • Lead site EHS Managers, their teams, and plant leadership in maintaining compliance through audits, inspections, assessments, recordkeeping, reporting, and verification of program effectiveness.
  • Partner with plant teams to develop, implement, maintain and continuously improve Safety Management Systems, including employee participation, hazard analyses, safe operating procedures, risk management, training, and communication programs.

  • Evaluate regulatory changes, emerging technologies, and industry best practices to identify opportunities for risk reduction and safety performance improvement.
  • Support capital planning and resource allocation by identifying safety-related needs, prioritizing them, and securing support for key compliance and risk reduction initiatives. Represent the EHS function in obtaining approval for needed capital and expenses to address EHS matters.

jobs.excerpt: POSITION: Senior Microsoft 365 Engineer (Identity, Endpoint & Compliance) We’re hiring the engineer who’ll own the Microsoft 365 platform at WellStreet, in an environment where identity and data governance are HIPAA obligations and not checkboxes.
jobs.description:
POSITION: Senior Microsoft 365 Engineer (Identity, Endpoint & Compliance)

We’re hiring the engineer who’ll own the Microsoft 365 platform at WellStreet, in an environment where identity and data governance are HIPAA obligations and not checkboxes. The governance you put in place is what we’ll run on, and how it gets managed is yours to define.

A week in this job:

Monday you’re designing the sensitivity label taxonomy and the DLP policies that enforce it across Exchange, SharePoint and Teams. Tuesday a clinical vendor needs SSO and SCIM, so you stand it up, and you’re the one who catches that their deprovisioning webhook never fires. Wednesday you close quarterly access reviews on privileged groups, driven off a Graph script you wrote instead of a spreadsheet somebody emails around. Thursday a Critical CVE lands from SecOps and you own the triage and the clock. Friday you take the Intune configuration that has only ever existed in an admin center and get it into the repo.

What you’ll own:

  • Entra ID: tenant architecture, Conditional Access, hybrid identity, privileged access, password protection and SSPR, access reviews
  • Intune: tenant configuration across Windows, macOS, iOS and Android. Compliance and configuration profiles, security baselines, Autopilot, update rings, app packaging.
  • Exchange Online, Teams and SharePoint: tenant configuration, mail flow, transport rules
  • Purview: DLP, sensitivity labeling, retention, audit configuration, eDiscovery, and HIPAA and HITRUST control mapping
  • Enterprise Applications: SSO and SCIM across the portfolio, plus the standard that no app touching PHI runs on standalone credentials
  • Defender: endpoint detection and response on every managed device, Defender for Office 365 anti-phishing and threat investigation, and the unified alert view across the M365 estate. Defender for Servers, Defender for Cloud, and Defender for Identity — the workload security surface — sit with infrastructure.
  • Vulnerability response: CVE triage from SecOps, remediation tracking, weekly report
  • The application portfolio: an accurate catalog, runbooks that work, and the vendors in your domain held to their SLAs and their BAAs

Where the lines are:

Your world is Microsoft 365 and the people who use it: identity for humans, endpoints, collaboration, and governance of the data your users create. Azure cloud infrastructure, the applications running in it, and workload identity sit with our infrastructure side. Entra ID is shared, since it’s identity for both halves, and we split it by what the identity represents — people are yours, machines are theirs. The same split carries into Defender: endpoint and email protection are yours, workload protection on Servers, Cloud, and Identity is theirs.

This job has depth, autonomy and a lot of engineering in it, but the depth runs toward M365 and not toward Azure. If you’d rather be building infrastructure, we’d both prefer to find out now.

How we work, and where we’re going:

Today this tenant is managed largely by clicking in admin centers. That’s what we’re hiring you to change.

We’re building toward version-controlled, API-driven management in an Azure DevOps repo, with Graph and PowerShell as the primary instruments, app-only auth and Key Vault instead of interactive logins, and Python or declarative tooling where they earn their place. We have no illusions about how far that goes, since parts of the M365 surface have solid config-as-code coverage today and parts don’t. What we’re after is that opening a portal becomes a deliberate exception.

We’re not asking for prior GitOps-on-M365 experience. That market barely exists and the tooling is mid-shift. We’re asking for the instinct and the judgment; the specific tooling we’ll work out together.

We use AI heavily across engineering, administration and documentation, and we expect fluency with it, including a clear sense of what has to be reviewed before it touches a tenant holding PHI.

What we need:

  • Five or more years in M365, identity or security engineering, with tenant-level depth in Entra ID and Intune
  • Real Purview configuration experience: writing DLP policies, labeling, retention, eDiscovery. Not just familiarity.
  • Microsoft Graph and PowerShell fluency. This is the one hard technical gate. You automate by default and you’ve built real things against the API. Python is a plus.
  • Version control is where your work lives, and branches and pull requests are normal practice for you
  • You’ve worked against a regulated framework, whether HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2 or PCI, and you can explain a control instead of just naming it
  • You use AI daily and can say where you trust it and where you check it

Nice to have:

Terraform, Bicep or Azure DevOps pipelines. Any exposure to declarative M365 management: Microsoft365DSC, a Terraform M365 provider, the Graph Tenant Configuration Management APIs. Healthcare IT. Owning a vulnerability or patch compliance program. FreshService or a comparable ITSM. ITIL v4. SC-200, SC-300, SC-400, MS-102, MD-102.

Why take this job:

Real platform ownership, plus the mandate and the backing to build an engineering practice around it: version control, review and automation in place of tribal knowledge and portal archaeology. You’re the first dedicated hire for this function, so you’re setting standards instead of inheriting a decade of somebody else’s. As we add engineers, this seat is the obvious lead.

About WellStreet Urgent Care

WellStreet Urgent Care is committed to providing the highest quality patient and customer care. Our technology team plays an important role in supporting the people, systems, and operations that allow our urgent care centers to deliver exceptional service to our patients and communities.

In addition to the above requirements, WellStreet is looking for team members with the following qualities:

  • A positive attitude toward patients, families, and coworkers.
  • Willingness to go the extra mile to create an outstanding experience for customers and to train and lead the center team to do the same.
  • A desire to work in concert with others in an upbeat and supportive atmosphere while reinforcing the WellStreet mission to provide uncompromising service.
  • A compelling desire to serve others, improve your community's health, and have fun every day.

  • Experience with hardware peripherals such as card readers, barcode scanners, receipt printers, and cash drawers.

jobs.description:
Circle (NYSE: CRCL) is one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies, building the foundation of a more open, global economy through digital assets, payment applications, and programmable blockchain infrastructure. Circle’s platform includes the world’s largest regulated stablecoin network anchored by USDC, Circle Payments Network for global money movement, and Arc, an enterprise-grade blockchain designed to become the Economic OS for the internet. Enterprises, financial institutions, and developers use Circle to power trusted, internet-scale financial innovation. Learn more at .

What you’ll be part of:

Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we're expanding into some of the world's strongest jurisdictions. Speed and efficiency are motivators for our success and our employees live by our company values: High Integrity, Future Forward, Multistakeholder, Mindful, and Driven by Excellence. We have built a flexible work environment where new ideas are encouraged and everyone is a stakeholder.

About the team

Every Circle product depends on this team to answer two questions: who is making a request, and what should they be allowed to do?

We build the platform behind customer identity and access for Circle Hub, Circle Mint, Custody, the Cross-Chain Payments Network, and the Developer Console. Our systems handle sign-up and sign-in, sessions and API credentials, service-to-service authentication, enterprise SSO, organizations and workspaces, user and role management, and the Policy Engine that governs approvals and access for money movement across products.


The next chapter is extending those capabilities to AI agents. Agents will need identities of their own, carefully bounded authority, short-lived credentials, and audit trails that connect every action back to the person or organization responsible for it.

This is a product and platform engineering team—not an IT access-administration function. The systems we build sit at the intersection of customer experience, security, reliability, and financial risk.


The role

We are looking for a hands-on engineering manager who has built identity or authorization systems at scale and can lead a team through significant platform change. You will set the technical direction for authentication, authorization, customer and emerging agent identity capabilities. You will manage and grow a team, partner closely with Security and product teams, and stay close to the work through design reviews, code reviews, debugging, incident response, and occasional implementation with a strong AI focus. This is both a people-management and technical role. You will be expected to make architecture decisions, explain trade-offs clearly, and create the conditions for the team to execute well. You will work closely with the team’s Staff Engineer and Team Lead, and help the broader organization understand how identity works at Circle.


What you will do

  • Own the technical vision, architecture, and roadmap for Circle’s identity and access platform.
  • Manage, coach, and grow a team of backend and frontend engineers. Set clear expectations, give direct feedback, develop senior engineers into technical leaders, and hire well.
  • Stay close to the code and systems. Lead technical designs, review critical code paths, debug production issues with the team, participate in incident response, and build prototypes when that is the fastest way to make progress.
  • Partner with Security, Product, Onboarding, Risk, and product engineering teams that integrate with identity.
  • Turn competing requests into a sequenced roadmap and explain the trade-offs behind it.
  • Run the team’s delivery process, including planning, scoping, migrations, cutovers, rollback plans, and honest status reporting.
  • Improve the team’s engineering practices, operational readiness, and ability to provide reliable platform capabilities to the rest of Circle.

What we are looking for

  • Experienced manager. You have at least three years of experience managing software engineers, including hiring, performance management, coaching, and developing senior individual contributors. You have led a team through a significant migration, re-platforming, or architectural change.
  • Deep identity or authorization experience. You have substantial hands-on experience building identity, authentication, authorization, or access-control systems at scale. Your background may include OAuth 2.x and OIDC, SAML and enterprise SSO, session and token design, API credentials, service or workload identity, MFA and passkeys, or policy and entitlement engines.
  • Strong architectural judgment. You have designed a system that other teams built on. You can explain the important trade-offs, how you managed migration and adoption, and what you would change if you were designing it again today.
  • Still technical. You stay close to production systems, read code and designs critically, and can help debug a difficult authentication or authorization issue. Recently, you have designed, prototyped, reviewed, or shipped production code.
  • Security-minded operator. You have dealt with real world Identity, Auth/Authz security problems and changed the design or operating model as a result. You understand that security monitoring requires more than tracking errors and latency.
  • Clear communicator. You write design documents people can use, explain complex systems plainly, and give leadership a direct answer with a recommendation attached.

Especially valuable for this role

  • Direct experience with Okta, Auth0, or an equivalent customer identity platform, including hosted-versus-custom architecture decisions, organization-level policies, or extensibility mechanisms.
  • Experience with AI agent identity, delegated authorization, workload identity, service identity, or other non-human identity systems.
  • A clear point of view on agent registration and lifecycle, delegation chains, least privilege, token scoping, revocation, auditability, and how to preserve accountability when an agent acts on behalf of a person or organization.
  • Experience building or operating systems where software agents or automated services can take consequential actions under bounded authority.

We do not expect this area to have a settled playbook. We do expect you to be comfortable designing secure systems in an emerging space and to understand the difference between an agent’s identity, the authority delegated to it, and the credentials it uses at runtime.


Nice to have

  • Experience in fintech, crypto, payments, or another regulated environment where KYC/KYB, entitlements, auditability, and operational controls are part of the product.
  • Familiarity with relevant identity and authorization patterns, including on-behalf-of token exchange, MCP authorization, SPIFFE/SPIRE, workload identity federation, agent registries, or policy engines such as OPA or Cedar.
  • Experience with Java or Kotlin backend systems and modern TypeScript frontend applications.
  • Experience leading a geographically distributed team.

Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives.

We are an innovative global healthcare company, committed to transforming the lives of people with immune challenges, rare diseases and blood disorders, cancers, and neurological disorders. From R&D to sales, our talented teams work together, revolutionizing treatment, continually improving products, understanding unmet needs, and connecting communities. Bilingual Medical Administrative Coordinator

About the Company

Our client is a growing U.S.-based healthcare support organization that provides remote administrative and operational assistance to medical practices across the United States.

The company partners with healthcare professionals to simplify administrative processes, improve practice efficiency, and ensure that medical teams can focus more of their time on patient care.

Its remote workforce supports essential healthcare operations, including patient documentation, insurance coordination, authorization requests, and provider-related administrative processes.

With an emphasis on accuracy, reliable communication, and efficient workflows, the organization continues expanding its remote support teams to meet the needs of healthcare providers across different medical specialties.

About the Role

We are seeking Bilingual Medical Administrative Coordinators to provide remote operational and administrative support to U.S.-based healthcare practices.

In this position, you will help medical teams manage patient information, coordinate insurance-related processes, maintain electronic health records, and support documentation required for prescriptions, authorizations, and provider enrollment.

You will interact with healthcare providers, insurance representatives, pharmacies, and patients to ensure administrative requests are handled accurately and efficiently.

This opportunity is ideal for someone with previous medical administration or healthcare support experience, strong organizational skills, and the ability to communicate professionally in both English and Spanish.

What You'll Do

Medical Records & Patient Information

  • Review and update patient demographic information in electronic health record systems.

  • Maintain accurate and organized EMR/EHR documentation.

  • Upload and organize laboratory reports, referrals, clinical notes, and other medical documents.

  • Verify patient insurance eligibility and benefit information.

  • Identify missing or incomplete records and coordinate necessary updates.

  • Support accurate and confidential handling of patient information.

Insurance Verification & Authorization Coordination

  • Assist with medical, procedure-related, and prescription prior authorizations.

  • Collect required information and supporting clinical documentation.

  • Submit authorization requests and monitor their progress.

  • Communicate with insurance carriers regarding pending decisions and additional requirements.

  • Follow up on authorization denials, appeals, and outstanding documentation.

  • Keep authorization records updated to support timely healthcare services.

Prescription & Pharmacy Administration

  • Coordinate administrative processing of prescription refill requests.

  • Communicate with pharmacies regarding medication-related requests.

  • Track prescription authorization statuses and pending responses.

  • Help resolve documentation issues that may delay prescription processing.

  • Keep healthcare teams informed about outstanding medication-related requests.

Provider Credentialing Support

  • Assist with administrative tasks related to provider enrollment with Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial insurance plans.

  • Update and maintain provider information in CAQH and other credentialing platforms.

  • Track credentialing applications and enrollment progress.

  • Monitor important provider documentation, including professional licenses, DEA registrations, and malpractice insurance.

  • Help identify upcoming credential expirations and outstanding enrollment requirements.

Healthcare Administrative Operations

  • Communicate with patients, providers, pharmacies, and insurance companies.

  • Maintain organized records of requests, updates, and follow-up activities.

  • Support daily administrative processes across medical practices.

  • Coordinate outstanding tasks to help reduce administrative delays.

  • Handle protected health information responsibly and maintain patient confidentiality.

Qualifications

Required

  • At least 1 year of relevant experience in medical administration, medical reception, healthcare virtual assistance, medical records, prior authorizations, credentialing, or a related healthcare support position.

  • Advanced English proficiency (C1/C2) and fluent Spanish, both written and spoken.

  • Experience verifying patient insurance eligibility and benefits.

  • Familiarity with Electronic Medical Records (EMR) or Electronic Health Records (EHR) systems.

  • Understanding of healthcare administrative procedures and medical documentation.

  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Ability to manage multiple requests and deadlines.

  • Professional written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.

  • Commitment to protecting confidential patient information and maintaining accurate records.

Preferred

  • Previous experience supporting U.S.-based medical practices or healthcare providers.

  • Familiarity with medical or pharmacy prior authorization processes.

  • Experience with provider credentialing and insurance enrollment.

  • Knowledge of CAQH, Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial insurance requirements.

  • Understanding of HIPAA regulations and healthcare documentation standards.

What Makes a Strong Candidate?

We are particularly interested in professionals who demonstrate:

  • Accuracy: You carefully review patient records, insurance details, and medical documentation.

  • Organization: You can manage several administrative processes without losing track of important information.

  • Follow-through: You consistently monitor pending requests and take action when additional information is needed.

  • Communication: You interact professionally with healthcare teams, patients, and insurance representatives.

  • Adaptability: You can work across different administrative workflows and learn new procedures.

  • Confidentiality: You understand the importance of protecting sensitive healthcare information.

How Success Is Measured

  • Patient records and electronic medical documentation remain complete and accurate.

  • Insurance eligibility information is verified and updated appropriately.

  • Prior authorization requests are submitted and followed up on efficiently.

  • Prescription-related administrative requests are coordinated in a timely manner.

  • Provider credentialing documentation and enrollment records remain organized.

  • Pending requests are tracked and communicated effectively.

  • Medical teams receive reliable administrative support that contributes to efficient daily operations.

  • Patient information is handled according to applicable confidentiality and compliance requirements.

Why Join Us?

  • 100% remote opportunity supporting healthcare operations in the United States.

  • Join an expanding healthcare support organization.

  • Gain experience across multiple areas of medical administration.

  • Work with insurance verification, EMR/EHR systems, prior authorizations, and provider documentation.

  • Develop specialized skills in U.S. healthcare administrative processes.

  • Contribute to smoother operations for medical professionals and their patients.

Important Notes

  • Advanced English (C1/C2) and fluent Spanish are required.

  • Candidates must have at least 1 year of relevant healthcare administrative experience.

  • Experience with insurance verification and EMR/EHR systems is required.

  • Previous exposure to U.S. healthcare practices is highly valued.

  • The position requires availability during U.S. business hours.

  • This is an administrative support position; clinical responsibilities are not part of the role.

This is a fully remote position.

jobs.title: Azure Platform & DevOps Architect
jobs.excerpt: Fidus is a global high-tech design firm headquartered in Ottawa, with additional design centres in Kitchener-Waterloo and San Jose.
jobs.description:
Fidus is a global high-tech design firm headquartered in Ottawa, with additional design centres in Kitchener-Waterloo and San Jose. We specialize in leading-edge electronic product development, with hardware, embedded software, FPGA/ASIC, and signal integrity teams working together to design and deliver next-generation products for clients in emerging technology markets.

About the role

Fidus is hiring a Azure Platform & DevOps Architect to join our IT team. Your first priority will be LodeStar, our AI design platform: you will make sure it is secure, reliable and ready to support client-facing service commitments as it grows from an internal tool into a product.

Alongside LodeStar, you will own DevOps for Fidus, including our Atlassian suite (Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket), and help engineering teams across the company work more effectively through better tooling, workflows and automation. This is a hands-on senior role where you will work closely with the LodeStar build and product leads and with engineering teams across Fidus.

About LodeStar

LodeStar turns Fidus’s engineering design history into a searchable, human-in-the-loop system that helps our designers find parts, check schematics and, over time, generate design building blocks. It runs mainly on Azure, with some automation on on-premise Jenkins servers.

Make an Impact with US:

At Fidus, you'll work on high-speed, high-complexity electronic systems, often using emerging technologies before they reach the broader market. You'll collaborate across FPGA/DSP, hardware, embedded software, verification, SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical/thermal design as part of cross-functional teams delivering real products for our clients.

In practice, that means contributing to projects across Communications, Aerospace & Defence, Life Sciences and Medical Devices, Space and Satellite, Industrial Automation, Automotive, and Semiconductor engagements. You won't be limited to a single product or industry—your work will follow the technology, not just one roadmap.

Requirements

What you will do

LodeStar platform

  • Design, build and run LodeStar’s Azure infrastructure using Terraform(or similar), with separate development, test and production environments.
  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions and Jenkins, including automated testing, approval gates and rollback.
  • Run PostgreSQL in production, including backups, regular restore testing and performance tuning.
  • Monitor availability and performance, lead incident response, and define and report on service level objectives.
  • Secure the platform with Entra ID, least-privilege access, Key Vault and private networking, working with IT & Security on export-control and CMMC requirements.
  • Manage the infrastructure behind LodeStar’s AI services, including model API access, usage and cost.

Fidus DevOps and IT

  • Own administration of Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket, including access, permissions, single sign-on, licensing, apps, upgrades and backups.
  • Work with engineering, project management and operations teams to improve Jira workflows, automation, dashboards and reporting.
  • Keep Confluence organized and easy to use, with a clear space structure, templates and permissions.
  • Set and support DevOps standards across Fidus, including source control, branching and CI/CD practices.
  • Contribute as a member of the IT team, including change management, security reviews and shared on-call.

What you bring

  • 5+ years in platform engineering, DevOps or site reliability engineering, including at least 2 years supporting production workloads on Azure.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Terraform and infrastructure as code.
  • Experience building CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions and Jenkins, and working with containers (Docker, Azure Container Apps or AKS).
  • Experience administering Jira and Confluence, including workflow design, automation and permissions.
  • Production experience with PostgreSQL or a similar relational database.
  • Solid Linux administration and networking skills, including hybrid on-premise and cloud environments.
  • Working knowledge of cloud security and identity management.
  • Scripting skills in Python or Bash.
  • Experience with on-call support and incident management.
  • Clear communication with both technical and non-technical colleagues.

Nice to have

  • Experience operating AI or LLM-based applications.
  • Experience in regulated environments such as CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, export controls or Canada’s Controlled Goods Program.
  • Microsoft Azure (AZ-104, AZ-400 or AZ-500), HashiCorp Terraform Associate or Atlassian certifications.
  • Experience at an engineering services or electronics design company.

How we work

You will be part of a small, collaborative team with regular standups and async communication on Teams. The role is remote, with occasional travel to Ottawa, and includes business-hours on-call on a shared rotation.

Eligibility

This role involves access to systems that may hold export-controlled technical data. Candidates must be eligible for Fidus’s export-control screening and, in Canada, a Controlled Goods Program security assessment.

Benefits

This role is being posted to fill an existing vacancy.

Annual base salary ranges from $120,000 to $155,000 CAD. The final offer within this range takes into account the variations in knowledge, skills, experience, and market conditions, and with consideration to internal equity.

Our competitive compensation package also includes a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, matching GRSP contributions, annual profit-sharing bonus, along with other supplementary benefits.

We also recognize that candidates show interest throughout different career stages and welcome all applications. When there is a great fit, the level of the role may be shifted as applicable.

Curious what it's actually like to work here? Take a look at our Working at Fidus page.

About Fidus & Why Work Here

Since 2001, Fidus has completed over 4,000 projects for more than 400 customers across industries including Telecom/Datacom, Aerospace & Defence, Consumer, Semiconductors, Industrial/Automotive Controls, and Medical. As a Premier Adaptive Computing Partner for AMD North America, we combine deep technical expertise with industry-leading tools to solve complex design challenges.

Fidus designs high-speed, high-complexity electronic systems using emerging technologies, often well before they reach the broader market. Our teams work across FPGA/DSP, hardware, embedded software, verification, SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical/thermal design to deliver real products for our customers.

Our work spans space and satellite systems, next-generation communications and networking, high-performance compute and storage platforms, advanced video and imaging, and industrial, medical, and automotive systems. We are not tied to a single product or industry—our work follows the technology, not just one roadmap.

At Fidus, collaboration is at the core of how we work. We value openness, trust, and shared ownership, and we create an environment where people are encouraged to contribute ideas, learn from one another, and have a meaningful impact through the work they do.

If all of this excites you, has your attention, and you can’t wait to join our amazing team and work environment, then we want to hear from you!

Fidus has a commitment to ensure a fair and transparent recruitment process. Automated tools (including AI) support our initial screening of applicants against our job posting to identify candidates whose qualifications, experience, and skills align most closely with the position requirements. All further candidate assessments and final selection are conducted by our human recruitment team. AI does not make any final hiring decisions.

Thank you for your interest in Fidus. We welcome and encourage diverse candidates to apply. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. Fidus is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.
