The Underpayment Recovery Analyst is responsible for the timely and accurate review, identification, and resolution of underpaid hospital claims. This role plays a critical part in optimizing client reimbursement by conducting detailed analyses of claim-level payments, following up with payers, and preparing appeals to address single-instance and systemic underpayments. The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in hospital payer contracts, reimbursement methodologies, and denial management, and will contribute to internal performance targets and client satisfaction.

​​Role and Responsibilities​

  • CLAIMS REVIEW AND ANALYSIS
  • Perform detailed analysis of remittances, explanations of benefits (EOBs),payer correspondence, and account detail to identify underpayments or incorrect claim adjudications.
  • Evaluate claim payment variances against expected reimbursements based on client-specific contract terms.
  • Accurately identify and categorize underpayment types and root causes (e.g., pricing discrepancies, DRG/APC miscalculations, bundling errors, inappropriate denials).
  • PAYER FOLLOW UP AND APPEALS
  • Initiate rebilled or corrected claims and manage timely follow-up on outstanding underpaid or denied claims.
  • Prepare and submit detailed appeals with appropriate documentation and contract references to secure accurate reimbursement.
  • Track outcomes and escalate unresolved issues as needed.
  • CONTRACTUAL EXPERTISE
  • Interpret complex hospital managed care contracts, fee schedules, payer policies, and government payer reimbursement policies.
  • Validate expected reimbursement across multiple payer types (e.g., Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, Commercial).
  • ROOT CAUSE AND TREND IDENTIFICATION
  • Identify and document systemic payer issues and trends affecting reimbursement.
  • Partner with internal teams and client stakeholders to recommend process improvements, payer escalations, or system configuration changes.
  • PERFORMANCE QUALITY
  • Meet or exceed established internal Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) related to claims reviewed, identifications, recovery amounts, appeal turnaround times, and accuracy.
  • Maintain up-to-date and organized case documentation in internal systems and client-facing portals.

Qualifications

  • Experience in healthcare revenue cycle, with a strong focus on underpayment/zero balance review, and payer reimbursement analysis.
  • Understanding of hospital managed care contracts and reimbursement methodologies (e.g., DRG, APC, percent-of-charge, per diem).
  • Experience with contract modeling tools and hospital billing systems (e.g., Epic, Cerner, Meditech).
  • Knowledge of payer-specific policies, billing regulations, and denial types (technical and clinical), payer-specific portals and dispute resolution processes.
  • Knowledge of CMS, Medicare Advantage, and state Medicaid plan rules.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex data and identify trends or discrepancies.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel and other data analysis/reporting tools.

Mental and physical demands

  • This position will be exposed mainly to an indoor office environment and will be expected to work in or around computers and printers.
  • The nature of the work is sedentary, and the employee will be sitting most of the time.
  • Essential physical functions of the job include typing and the repetitive motion to utilize computer software and hardware continuously throughout the day.
  • Essential mental functions of this position include concentrating on analytical tasks, reading information, and verbal/written communication to others continuously throughout the day.

Related duties as assigned

  • This job description documents the general nature and level of work but is not intended to be a comprehensive list of activities, duties, or responsibilities required for this position. Consequently, employees may be asked to perform other duties as required.
  • Employees may also be asked to complete certain compliance requirements set forth by our Business Partners in the performance of their jobs including but not limited to requests for background and drug screenings and disclosures of personal health information or personally identifiable information. Exemptions as provided under the ADA and TITLE VII of the Civil Rights Act will be observed and followed.

jobs.description:
At Anchorage Digital, we are building the world’s most advanced digital asset platform for institutions to participate in crypto.
Anchorage Digital is a crypto platform that enables institutions to participate in digital assets through custody, staking, trading, governance, settlement, and the industry's leading security infrastructure. Home to Anchorage Digital Bank N.A., the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., Anchorage Digital also serves institutions through Anchorage Digital Singapore, Porto by Anchorage Digital, and other offerings.
The company is funded by leading institutions including Andreessen Horowitz, GIC, Goldman Sachs, KKR, and Visa, with its Series D valuation over $3 billion. Founded in 2017 in San Francisco, California, Anchorage Digital has offices in New York, New York; Porto, Portugal; Singapore; and Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Learn more at anchorage.com, on X @Anchorage, and on LinkedIn.

With the evolving landscape of digital threats and an increasing volume of sophisticated attacks by malicious actors, we have a security policy mandating all new hires complete an in-person onboarding process - no exceptions. Security is our foundation and we prioritize physical identity verification and secure IT setup. While our security and IT logistics require physical presence to protect our infrastructure from sophisticated global threats, this move is equally about our Village culture. We believe that a laptop can be shipped, but our culture cannot.

Anchorage Digital is seeking a Product Manager to help build the leading RWA tokenization hub on Anchorage's core platform. Reporting to the Head of Tokenization, this role sits at the intersection of regulated capital markets and on-chain infrastructure: partnering directly with the business lead on product design, owning the technical roadmap with engineering, and shaping both the investor and the issuer experience across money market funds, tokenized MMFs, broker-dealer activity, transfer agency, fixed income, and equities.

You’ll partner with the Head of Tokenization to co-own product design and the end-to-end technical roadmap for Anchorage’s RWA tokenization hub, turning business strategy and client demand into prioritized product bets. You’ll design both sides of the platform: how issuers onboard, structure, mint, and service tokenized assets, and how institutional investors discover, allocate to, settle, and report on them. Your work will span money market funds (including tokenized MMFs), broker-dealer activity, transfer agency, fixed income, and equities, with a focus on building reusable foundations that work across asset classes instead of one-off integrations. You’ll work closely with engineering to scope problems and build solutions together, translating between technical, business, and regulatory concepts. You’ll also meet directly with issuers and investors to understand their needs and test product direction, and you’ll join the commercial team on live deals as the product expert who can go deep on both regulatory structure and on-chain mechanics.

This role will accelerate the candidate into a leading product voice at the intersection of banking, capital markets, and tokenization.

Below, we define our Factors of Growth & Impact to help Anchorage Villagers to better measure impact and articulate coaching, feedback, and the rich and rewarding learning that happens while exploring, developing, and mastering the capabilities and contributions within and outside of the Member of Product, Tokenization role:

Technical Skills:

  • Define tokenization product strategy, primitives, and roadmap across issuance, lifecycle management, custody, settlement, reporting, and investor/issuer workflows.
  • Translate complex regulatory, capital markets, and blockchain constraints into clear product requirements.

Complexity and Impact of Work:

  • Lead product delivery across a multi-asset-class roadmap (MMFs, commodities, fixed income, equities, etc) in a highly regulated environment.
  • Drive outcomes that scale issuer onboarding, deepen the investor experience, and build reusable primitives rather than bespoke integrations.

Organizational Knowledge:

  • Navigate OCC/banking-grade governance, controls, and risk management expectations.
  • Build operating rhythms with engineering, legal, compliance, and client-facing teams that keep delivery moving without compromising controls.

Communication and Influence:

  • Translate fluently between business and engineering audiences in both directions.
  • Influence senior stakeholders (issuers, investors, internal leadership) through crisp narratives and tradeoff framing
  • Credibly represent the product in front of institutional issuers and investors; convert what you hear in those rooms into roadmap signal.

You may be a fit for this role if you have:

  • A track record owning a technical product roadmap end-to-end in regulated financial services (capital markets, payments, asset management, or banking).
  • A deep working knowledge of blockchain infrastructure and institutional digital asset products
  • Demonstrated ability to translate between technical and business audiences, not just document the hand-off, but make both sides sharper.
  • Experience shipping platform products with meaningful partner, regulatory, and engineering dependencies.
  • Comfort and appetite for client-facing work, meeting with institutional prospects and clients to discover needs, demo product direction, and influence commercial outcomes.
  • Bias for ownership and execution in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
  • At least two of the following three: (a) direct experience with tokenization, tokenized MMFs, transfer agency, broker-dealer tech, or securities issuance platforms; (b) prior work at a regulated financial institution, trust company, or capital markets infrastructure firm; or (c) prior experience in a product role that was explicitly commercial-adjacent (solutions, pre-sales, or client-facing PM).

Although not a requirement, bonus points if:

  • You have product design judgment across two-sided experiences (investor-facing and issuer-facing).
  • Claude or other AI tools have become part of your core tools for work.
  • You have strong opinions on how capital markets will move on-chain.
  • You have navigated a regulator directly on a product launch.

About Anchorage Digital: Who we are

The Anchorage Village, what we call our team, brings together the brightest minds from platform security, financial services, and distributed ledger technology to provide the building blocks that empower institutions to safely participate in the evolving digital asset ecosystem. As a diverse team of more than 600 members, we are united in one common goal: building the future of finance by providing the foundation upon which value moves safely in the new global economy.
Anchorage Digital is committed to being a welcoming and inclusive workplace for everyone, and we are intentional about making sure people feel respected, supported, and connected at work—regardless of who you are or where you come from. We value and celebrate our differences and we believe being open about who we are allows us to do the best work of our lives.
Anchorage Digital is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or veteran status. Anchorage Digital considers qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with other legal requirements. “Anchorage Digital” refers to services that are offered either through Anchorage Digital Bank National Association, an OCC-chartered national trust bank, or Anchorage Lending CA, LLC a finance lender licensed by the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation, License No. 60DBO-11976, or Anchorage Digital Singapore Pte Ltd, a Singapore private limited company, all wholly-owned subsidiaries of Anchor Labs, Inc., a Delaware corporation.

jobs.excerpt: AI macht uns schneller.  Das Denken nimmt sie uns nicht ab.
jobs.description:
AI macht uns schneller. Das Denken nimmt sie uns nicht ab.
Was AI produziert, überprüfen wir. Für alles, was rausgeht, stehen wir gerade.
Beim Ausprobieren sind wir schnell, beim Ausliefern gründlich.

Du liest ein Paper und willst wissen, ob die Idee hält. Also klonst du das Repo. Läuft es nicht, folgst du dem Stacktrace in den Quellcode. Und widersprechen die Daten deiner Hypothese, stutzt du kurz und freust dich: Jetzt wird es interessant. Ein schönes Ergebnis macht dich dagegen erst mal misstrauisch. Zufall? Bug? Oder hält es?

Bei smartclip arbeitest du mit Messdaten von Dutzenden Millionen Geräten, eigener GPU-Infrastruktur und Sidekicks, unserer AI-Initiative für Wissensfragen und echte Workflows. Du verantwortest deine Fragestellung vom ersten Experiment bis zum belastbaren Prototyp. Den baut Engineering mit dir zum Produkt aus.

Unser Stack basiert auf Linux, Open Source und freier Software. Du kannst nachvollziehen, was unter der Haube passiert.

Deine Mission

Eine Stelle, zwei Schwerpunkte. Ob du einen vertiefst oder beide, entscheiden dein Können und deine Vorlieben. AI gehört immer dazu.

1. Knowledge Agents & Agentic Retrieval

Wie beantwortet ein Agent eine Frage, deren Antwort über Tausende Dokumente verteilt ist? Wie erkennt er Widersprüche zwischen Entwürfen und finalen Fassungen? Und wie belegt er seine Antworten zuverlässig?

  • Entwickle Agenten, die Informationen über große Dokumentbestände hinweg erschließen.

  • Untersuche, wie sich Vollständigkeit, Widersprüche und die Qualität von Quellen bewerten lassen.

  • Sorge dafür, dass Antworten nachvollziehbar bleiben und Unsicherheiten sichtbar werden.

2. Machine Learning at Scale

Wir messen das Werbegeschehen bei mehr als 150 TV-Sendern in Europa. Unser Ziel: lineares Fernsehen so planbar und messbar machen wie digitale Werbung.

  • Entwickle Prognosemodelle für die Leistung von Werbeblöcken.

  • Bewerte Unsicherheiten, Messfehler und die Aussagekraft deiner Modelle.

  • Verarbeite große Datenmengen mit Spark auf unserem Cluster und untersuche, wo Datenqualität oder Verarbeitung die Ergebnisse beeinflussen.

In beiden Bereichen machst du aus einer guten Frage etwas, das läuft:

  • Experimentiere und evaluiere: Formuliere Hypothesen, entwirf aussagekräftige Tests und lerne aus Ergebnissen, auch wenn diese nicht deine Erwartungen erfüllen.

  • Übernimm Verantwortung: Entwickle deinen Ansatz eigenständig bis zum belastbaren Prototyp. Hol dir einen zweiten Blick oder denk mit deinem Team am Whiteboard weiter.

  • Arbeite mit Engineering: Begleite die Überführung deines Prototyps in ein Produkt und bringe dein Wissen über Problem und Lösung ein.

  • Unterstütze andere Teams: Bewerte Datenfragen, zeige sinnvolle Einsatzmöglichkeiten von AI auf und liefere je nach Bedarf eine fundierte Empfehlung oder einen Prototyp.

Deine Skills

  • Fundierte technische Grundlagen: Bring Kenntnisse in Informatik, Softwareentwicklung oder Data Science mit – erworben durch Studium, Promotion oder praktische Erfahrung. Du kannst deine Methodenwahl begründen und Ergebnisse kritisch bewerten.

  • Verständnis für AI: Du musst keine Modelle in PyTorch trainieren. Du kannst aber den Unterschied zwischen Prefill und Decode erklären und wie dieser für Latenz und Kosten relevant ist.

  • Eigenständiges AI-native Development: Nutze Coding-Agenten, um schneller zu entwickeln. Validiere den generierten Code, teste die Ergebnisse und verstehe, wie deine Anwendung und ihre Komponenten funktionieren.

  • Strukturiertes Experimentieren: Formuliere klare Specs, definiere eine Definition of Done und prüfe mit passenden Tests und Evaluationen, ob deine Umsetzung das richtige Problem löst.

  • Offene Zusammenarbeit: Teile Wissen, diskutiere technische Entscheidungen und gib respektvolles, direktes Feedback.

Ein Plus, kein Muss: Erfahrung mit NLP/Computerlinguistik, Agentic Retrieval oder der Entwicklung von LLM-Agenten.

Unser Stack

  • Knowledge Agents: Python (Pydantic AI), TypeScript, vLLM/SGLang

  • Daten und Pipelines: Spark, Trino, StarRocks, Postgres und Prefect

  • Infrastruktur und Observability: OpenTelemetry, Docker/Kubernetes

Kennst du eher Ray, LangChain, Airflow, passt das genauso: Die Konzepte zählen, nicht die Logos.

Was dich bei uns erwartet

  • Remote Work mit gezielten Treffen: Wir arbeiten überwiegend remote und kommen gelegentlich für Workshops, Team-Sessions und den gemeinsamen Austausch in unserem Tech-Office in Berlin zusammen. Außerdem veranstalten wir über das Jahr verteilt Team-Events, darunter unser jährliches Company Offsite, das jedes Jahr an einer anderen Location in Deutschland stattfindet. Die Bereitschaft, für diese Treffen anzureisen und daran teilzunehmen, gehört zur Rolle.

  • Eigenverantwortung statt Mikromanagement: Übernimm Verantwortung für deine Themen und bringe sie selbstständig voran.

  • Build > Talk: Früh ausprobieren, früh danebenliegen, früh dazulernen.

  • Hohe Ansprüche, wenig Ego: Wir geben direktes Feedback und arbeiten offen und respektvoll zusammen.

  • Weiterentwicklung: Nutze Hackathons, Konferenzen und Community-Austausch, um fachlich dazuzulernen.

Und natürlich stimmen auch die Rahmenbedingungen: 30 Urlaubstage plus frei am 24. und 31. Dezember, Smart Fridays mit der Möglichkeit einer Vier-Tage-Woche, Deutschlandticket und JobRad, Sport- und Gesundheitsangebote, Unterstützung für die mentale Gesundheit, Corporate Benefits, Zugang zu RTL+ und vieles mehr.

Dein Lebenslauf ist nur der Anfang.

Was uns mehr interessiert als dein Lebenslauf: ein Portfolio, ein Side Project oder ein Demo-Repo – etwas, das zeigt, wie du technische Probleme angehst und Lösungen umsetzt.

🤖 AI Disclaimer: AI durfte mitdenken, aber nicht das letzte Wort haben. Das behalten wir uns vor.

Position: Executive Assistant/ Bookkeeper

Salary: AUD $1,800/month salary

Working Hours & Conditions: Sydney business hours, Monday to Friday

ROLE OVERVIEW:

The Executive Assistant / Bookkeeper (EA/BK) serves as a dual-impact operational backbone for the company, balancing day-to-day corporate financial reconciliation with high-level administrative governance. Reporting directly to the Philippines-based Senior Accountant for bookkeeping duties and to the executive leadership team for administrative functions, this role ensures seamless accounting workflow, pristine audit trails, and strict compliance with Australian regulatory standards. Ultimately, this position exists to free up leadership bandwidth while keeping the company's financial and governance operations organized, accurate, and predictable.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Bookkeeping

  • Reconcile bank, Shopify and company card transactions in Xero daily, match customer receipts to invoices, and follow up missing receipts from card holders
  • Review and correct coding of supplier invoices processed through Lightyear (AP automation), and maintain supplier coding defaults
  • Check invoices are approved in line with our approval policy, and support the weekly supplier pay run, including verifying supplier bank details before approval
  • Reconcile supplier statements against Xero, and chase outstanding supplier invoices to minimise month-end accruals
  • Monitor the accounts payable and supplier inboxes and respond to payment enquiries within 24 hours using standard templates, escalating non-standard matters
  • First-pass checks of staff expense claims against policy before payment
  • Set up new suppliers and customers, including credit applications, onboarding forms, and ABN and bank detail verification
  • Weekly review and recoding of transactions so revenue, costs, intercompany balances and balance sheet items are correctly classified
  • Check and correct GST coding, escalating queries for review

Executive and administrative support

  • General executive and administrative support to the leadership team
  • Board administration: compiling monthly board packs from contributors, preparing agendas, minutes and action trackers, and maintaining the board and shareholder document library
  • Secretarial support, including preparing documents for e-signature (DocuSign) and following up signatures
  • Preparing meeting agendas and supporting materials
  • Formatting PowerPoint presentations to a professional standard
  • Maintaining organised digital filing for financial and administrative records
  • Travel bookings and diary coordination for the leadership team, including capturing itineraries and tax invoices in Xero
  • Maintaining the compliance, insurance and contracts registers (renewal dates, certificates of currency) and sending reminders ahead of due dates
  • Ad hoc administrative and operational support

Requirements

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 2 years experience as Executive Assistant with Bookkeeping experience
  • Hands-on Xero experience (essential)
  • Experience with Australian GST and BAS-related transaction coding
  • Experience with AP automation tools (Lightyear or similar) and Shopify reconciliations (highly desirable)
  • Bank and card reconciliations across multiple entities (desirable)
  • Experience supporting a board or company secretary: board packs, minutes, registers (desirable)
  • Demonstrated discretion with confidential board, shareholder and financial information
  • Willingness to use AI and automation tools to streamline repetitive tasks
  • Strong Microsoft 365 skills, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook
  • Working hours aligned with Sydney business hours, Monday to Friday

bswift is a leading benefits administration company that specializes in providing tailored solutions for our clients. Our mission is to simplify the complex world of employee benefits and deliver exceptional service to our clients. We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented GRC Analyst to join our Information Security team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

The GRC Analyst is a member of the Information Security team and is responsible for supporting governance, risk, compliance, and client assurance activities. This role serves as a key partner to Sales, Client Experience, Legal, Product, and Information Security teams by responding to customer security inquiries, supporting audit and compliance efforts, and maintaining processes that support security and regulatory obligations.

The ideal candidate possesses a strong foundation in information security concepts, excellent written communication skills, and the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, concise, customer-friendly responses. This individual thrives in a deadline-driven environment, enjoys collaborating across teams, and demonstrates strong attention to detail, organization, and follow-through.

WHAT YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR (Essential Functions)

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Client Assurance & Security Questionnaire Management

  • Serve as a primary point of contact for client assurance requests, including security questionnaires, due diligence inquiries, RFP security sections, SOC reports, bridge letters, penetration test summaries, and other security-related documentation.
  • Review and respond to detailed client security questionnaires by interpreting requirements and providing accurate, defensible responses aligned with company policies and security practices.
  • Partner with Sales, Client Experience, Legal, Product, and Information Security teams to gather information and respond to customer security inquiries within established service-level expectations.
  • Utilize approved security questionnaire and AI-enabled response tools to draft and refine responses while ensuring accuracy, consistency, and appropriate disclosure of information.
  • Support the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of reusable security response content and documentation.

Risk, Compliance & Audit Support

  • Support internal and external audits, including SOC 2 and other compliance assessments, by coordinating evidence requests and assisting with control documentation.
  • Collect, organize, and maintain audit-ready evidence supporting compliance initiatives and recurring review activities.
  • Assist with governance, risk, and compliance processes designed to maintain adherence to security frameworks, internal controls, and regulatory requirements.
  • Support remediation efforts by tracking action items and partnering with stakeholders to ensure timely resolution of identified issues.

User Access Review Administration

  • Own and execute recurring User Access Reviews (UARs) for critical systems and applications.
  • Coordinate with system owners and managers to validate that user access remains appropriate and aligned with least-privilege principles.
  • Collect, maintain, and organize evidence supporting access review activities.
  • Track remediation actions resulting from access reviews and partner with business and technical stakeholders to resolve identified exceptions.

Contract Review & Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Support the review and negotiation of customer security addenda, contract language, and redlined security requirements.
  • Partner with Legal and Information Security stakeholders to evaluate proposed contractual obligations and recommend appropriate revisions.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to internal business teams by providing guidance related to security controls, compliance requirements, and customer assurance requests.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify and implement opportunities to improve processes, documentation, automation, and reporting across the Governance, Risk, and Compliance program.
  • Participate in broader governance and risk initiatives as security processes mature and become more automated.
  • Contribute to ongoing program enhancement efforts that improve operational efficiency, consistency, and overall customer experience.

WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED (Required Education and Experience)

  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Business Administration, Risk Management, Accounting, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and work experience.
  • Two (2) or more years of experience in information security, IT audit, governance, risk and compliance (GRC), security compliance, client assurance, or a related discipline.
  • Working knowledge of information security and compliance concepts including:
    • SOC 2
    • Access Management
    • Least Privilege
    • Segregation of Duties
    • Disaster Recovery
    • Data Protection
    • Security Testing and Controls
  • Experience interpreting questionnaires, gathering information from stakeholders, and preparing accurate and professional responses.
  • Strong written communication skills with the ability to explain technical and compliance concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Strong organizational, documentation, and follow-up skills.
  • Demonstrated initiative, accountability, and willingness to learn new technologies, products, and security requirements.

Skills & Abilities

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent interpersonal and collaboration skills.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive information.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams.
  • Ability to work independently while effectively partnering across departments.

NICE TO HAVE (Preferred Education and Experience)

  • Experience completing customer security questionnaires, due diligence requests, or security sections of RFPs.
  • Experience supporting SOC 2 audits, IT audits, or compliance assessments.
  • Experience administering access certification or user access review programs.
  • Experience reviewing security contract language, security addenda, or contract redlines in partnership with Legal teams.
  • Familiarity with GRC and security questionnaire management platforms such as SecurityPal, Archer, OneTrust, MetricStream, or similar tools.
  • Background in IT audit, SOC auditing, risk management, compliance, or related disciplines.
  • Experience in SaaS, healthcare technology, benefits administration, financial services, or other highly regulated industries.
  • Relevant certifications such as CISA, CRISC, Security+, CISSP, or similar credentials.

OTHER DUTIES

Minimal travel may be required.

jobs.excerpt: Metabase is the easiest way for people to get insights from their data, from tiny startups who get up and running quickly to major corporations with tens of thousands of users.
jobs.description:
Metabase is the easiest way for people to get insights from their data, from tiny startups who get up and running quickly to major corporations with tens of thousands of users. That's why people love us.
We bring data tools with the elegance and simplicity of consumer products to the crufty world of enterprise business intelligence. We provide an opinionated open source starting point for how companies should measure, analyze and share their data, which is used by tens of thousands of companies.

About the Role

    We’re looking for a Security Engineer with deep expertise in source code analysis and offensive product security research. You’ll dig into complex software architectures, trace how code behaves at runtime, uncover subtle vulnerabilities, and address the systemic flaws behind them.

    Embedded in our core engineering team, you’ll help shape security decisions from early design through release and adoption. This is a hands-on engineering and research role: you’ll combine your security expertise with frontier AI tools to find vulnerabilities, develop fixes, and make Metabase secure by default across its product, dependencies, and runtime.

Things you’ll do

  • Partner with engineers throughout feature development, bringing security expertise to design, implementation, release, and adoption.
  • Build security-focused features, lead security improvements across the codebase, and implement fixes that address root causes.
  • Use and evaluate advanced AI tools to scale code analysis, vulnerability research, and secure engineering practices.
  • Conduct offensive research into Metabase, develop proofs of concept, and validate vulnerabilities.
  • Assess findings based on exploitability and real-world impact, define clear remediation criteria, and verify that fixes are effective.
  • Turn individual findings into broader improvements that prevent entire classes of vulnerabilities.

What you bring

  • A demonstrated track record of finding and exploiting application vulnerabilities through source code analysis and hands-on research.
  • The ability to independently navigate unfamiliar codebases, understand complex architectures, and reason about runtime behavior and trust boundaries.
  • Experience with application security challenges, including authentication, authorization, injection, and unsafe handling of untrusted data.
  • Sound judgment about exploitability and real-world impact, and the ability to communicate findings and remediation options clearly.
  • Strong software engineering skills, including the ability to implement durable security fixes. Experience in Clojure, or a strong desire to learn.
  • A thoughtful approach to AI-assisted security work, using these tools to extend your expertise while independently validating their output.
  • Ownership and curiosity: you pursue difficult questions, collaborate closely with engineers, and follow findings through to resolution.
Compensation
The US base salary range for this role is $160K–$225K annually, plus equity and benefits.
Compensation is determined by role, level, location, and individual qualifications, including skills, experience, and scope of responsibility. Pay may vary by geographic location and other job-related factors.

Benefits
We offer meaningful equity and a comprehensive US benefits package, including fully employer-covered medical, dental, and vision insurance (with 75% coverage for dependents), a 401(k) with employer match available to enroll after the first 30 days, flexible and unlimited paid time off including sick time, and an asynchronous, remote-first environment.
We're a global team (50% outside the US), fully distributed (from Thailand to California), who get things done asynchronously, with plenty of uninterrupted time, supporting each other to do the best work of our careers. We offer flexibility (define your own schedule and work from wherever you want), autonomy, and an environment that fosters growth, learning, and development. We're relentlessly user-focused and believe in building long-term value, not short-term hacks. And we raised a $30M Series B to take our approach to the next level for years to come.

jobs.description:
About the Role:

WEX is transforming how businesses manage spend and fleets—with a vision beyond traditional fueling through a growing set of payment, discounting, and platform capabilities built on shared platform investments.

We are looking for an experienced, strategic, and execution-driven Senior Product Manager (Level 4) to own and scale our next generation of Merchant Product solutions. Sitting within the North American Mobility (NAM) Product Team, you will act as an emerging strategic leader and trusted influencer owning a significant set of initiatives aligned to our core merchant systems—including discount networks (such as the EDGE Savings Network), pricing programs, and merchant-to-fleet communication channels.

In this role, you will drive the full product lifecycle from ideation to market delivery, connecting deep customer insights to broader company strategy, and owning customer adoption, usage, and financial value. You will work closely with senior product leaders, engineering, design, and go-to-market teams to create capabilities that communicate dynamic pricing and discount programs to fleets, driving mutual value across our merchant and fleet ecosystems.


What You’ll Do:

  • Develop Bold Vision and Product Strategy: Act as an emerging strategic leader to develop a bold vision and clear priorities for WEX’s merchant product ecosystem. Shape product strategy across our portfolio of discounting solutions, identify market gaps, and serve as a strategic partner to senior leadership.
  • Own Product and Financial Outcomes: Drive the execution of complex merchant initiatives, owning customer and business outcomes. Proactively define input and output metrics, utilizing rigorous business modeling and OKRs to tell the performance story of your product and drive customer and financial outcomes.
  • Lead Deep Customer and Partner Discovery: Dive deep into user behaviors and establish ongoing relationships with key merchants and fleets. Integrate qualitative and quantitative insights to pinpoint top partner problems and guide core product trade-offs.
  • Drive Multi-Channel Experiences & Portal Enhancements: Own and optimize customer journeys as they utilize our discounting programs across digital portals and platforms. Streamline onboarding workflows, automate administrative operations, and represent merchant product priorities within broader platform initiatives to reduce friction.
  • Design & Execute Iterative Experiments: Formulate hypotheses and design test-and-learn experiments to improve system administration, portal usability, and customer workflows, driving measurable adoption and delivering on key OKRs.
  • Partner & Influence Cross-Functionally: Build trust and facilitate alignment across Digital, Technology, Commercial, Risk, and Operations teams to ensure technical, operational, and financial systems are fully aligned and revenue is secure.
  • Manage Full Business & System Lifecycle: Oversee the evolution of merchant capabilities from initial ideation to a scalable, repeatable model. Detail how data flows through core systems and merchant-specific platforms, ensuring operational readiness at every stage.

Merchant Product Specifics:

  • Collaborate Across Customer-Facing Product Teams: Partner closely with adjacent WEX product owners who manage mobile apps, web portals, and communication channels to ensure they understand, align on, and prioritize the necessary features and configurations required to support seamless driver and fleet manager discounting and incentive use cases.
  • Align Go-to-Market & Value Communications: Coordinate across marketing, product marketing, customer service, and commercial teams to ensure consistent external communications that clearly articulate the value of WEX discounting programs to fleets.
  • Expand Platform & Merchant Communication Capabilities: Drive enhancements to our core pricing, discounting, and merchant platforms to enable partners to configure, manage, and effectively communicate dynamic, self-set discounts directly to participating fleets.
  • Design & Execute Fuel-Saving Behavioral Experiments: Formulate hypotheses and run test-and-learn experiments to understand when, where, and how drivers and fleet managers utilize pricing and discount information, optimizing their decision-making for maximum fuel savings.

What You Bring:

  • Minimum of 5+ years: of professional Product Management experience (or 8+ years of professional experience with significant tenure in product leadership), ideally within payment platforms, fintech, merchant services, or B2B platforms.
  • Strategic Leadership: Proven experience owning and strategically leading a significant set of initiatives aligned to a major product area or platform capability.
  • Technical Domain Expertise: Strong expertise in systems thinking and platform strategy, with a background in payment platform products, merchant ecosystems, APIs, and partner integrations.
  • Metrics & Outcomes Focus: Proven track record of defining and leveraging metrics/OKRs to tell a product's performance story, justify strategic priorities, and deliver customer and financial outcomes.
  • Roadmapping & Scaling: Strong strategic planning and roadmapping capabilities, with the ability to define repeatable patterns from one-off integrations and establish clear development phases.
  • Collaborative Influence: Excellent collaborative influence and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to build trust, facilitate difficult conversations, and align stakeholders.
  • Data-Driven Insights: Insights-proficient and highly comfortable utilizing qualitative and quantitative data and interactive tools to drill down and make informed product decisions.
  • Mentorship: Proven leadership and mentorship skills, with the ability to guide and role-model discovery methods and strategic thinking for junior PMs.

Nice to Have:

  • Direct experience with core pricing, discounting, or ledger systems.
  • Fluency running GTM experiments, channel testing, or behavioral A/B tests.
  • Master’s Degree in business, technology, or a related field.

Why This Role Matters:

WEX is expanding its merchant systems and platform capabilities, unlocking critical growth opportunities through our discounting and pricing ecosystems. This role will help shape how we:

  • Deepen Relationships: Deepen connections between merchants and fleets by facilitating seamless, dynamic value exchange and direct communications.
  • Simplify Savings: Simplify and optimize how fleets discover, utilize, and maximize savings programs.
  • Drive Cross-Functional Alignment: Drive cross-functional alignment across digital interfaces, core processing layers, commercial, and risk teams to scale unified solutions.
  • Empower Partners: Ensure that merchants have comprehensive, flexible tools to configure discounts and attract fleet volumes, establishing repeatable platform patterns.

What Success Looks Like:

  • Strategic Roadmapping: You define and drive the strategic roadmap for a portion of WEX Merchant Products, translating a bold vision into market-ready features and platform capabilities.
  • Cross-Functional Trusted Partnership: You foster close, collaborative relationships with cross-functional partners, ensuring operational, technical, and risk readiness for new discounting schemes and merchant configurations.
  • Behavioral Experiments: You leverage qualitative and quantitative insights to design experiments that increase merchant-to-fleet communication effectiveness and optimize driver savings.
  • Mentorship and Alignment: You act as a trusted leader and influencer, mentoring junior product managers and driving alignment across tech, commercial, and customer-facing product teams.
The base pay range represents the anticipated low and high end of the pay range for this position. Actual pay rates will vary and will be based on various factors, such as your qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role. Base pay is one component of WEX's total compensation package. Most sales positions are eligible for commission under the terms of an applicable plan. jobs.description:

Overview:

Overview

The Enterprise Resilience Role helps strengthen the organization’s ability to anticipate, withstand, respond to, recover from, and adapt to cyber, technology, operational, and third-party disruptions. The role connects technical recoverability with business continuity and critical business service outcomes. It partners across Cyber Security, Information Technology, Disaster Recovery, Business Continuity, Emergency Management, business operations, and vendor management to establish consistent resilience requirements, validate recovery capabilities, track gaps, and drive measurable improvements.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can work across technical and business teams, bring structure to a developing enterprise program, and translate resilience risks into clear actions and decisions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Enterprise Resilience Program, including governance, standards, procedures, playbooks, reporting, and program documentation.
  • Help identify and maintain Critical Business Services and map the people, processes, technology, data, facilities, and third parties required to deliver them.
  • Partner with business and technology owners to define and validate impact tolerances, recovery time objectives, recovery point objectives, minimum service levels, and recovery priorities.
  • Plan, coordinate, and document resilience assessments, business impact analyses, tabletop exercises, disaster recovery tests, cyber recovery exercises, and simulations.
  • Track findings, risks, decisions, owners, due dates, and corrective actions through closure; identify recurring themes and escalate material gaps when needed.
  • Enhance backup and recovery capabilities, including Rubrik, Azure-native backups, SQL-native backups, and Veeam.
  • Improve ransomware-resilient recovery capabilities through immutable backups, clean-point validation, data-integrity checks, malware-aware recovery practices, and secure restoration workflows.
  • Help build and mature the isolated recovery environment, including automation of restoration testing and repeatable validation of recoverability.
  • Participate in disaster recovery exercises with infrastructure, application, security, and business teams to confirm that systems, data, integrations, and business processes can be restored and validated.
  • Coordinate cyber, business, and enterprise tabletop exercises to test decision-making, communications, downtime procedures, manual workarounds, escalation paths, and recovery actions.

Responsibilities include access management, vulnerability management, change management, logging, and backup and recovery controls.

jobs.title: Head of Strategic Partnerships
jobs.excerpt: Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.
jobs.description:
Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors. This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock, TPG (The Rise Fund), SoftBank, Glynn Capital, NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more.

About the role

The Head of Strategic Partnerships owns a vital piece of Human Interest's most important growth channel: expanding our ecosystem of partners who put our retirement platform in front of millions of small and medium-sized businesses. Reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer, you will lead the team to identify, pursue, and close strategic partnerships across payroll providers, benefits brokers, accountants, financial institutions, PEOs, and embedded fintech distribution.

This is a leadership role focused on building, scaling, and driving the strategic partnership ecosystem. While hands-on, the focus is on organizational strategy, team mentorship, and driving cross-functional success. You will be responsible for signing complex, multi-year agreements with some of Human Interest’s largest and most important partners.

The role is equal parts strategist, dealmaker, and operator. You'll be just as comfortable modeling the economics of a new channel as you are in a room negotiating terms, and just as effective driving a deal across the finish line as you are shaping the partnership thesis with the CRO and the broader leadership team.

The person who thrives here is a natural hunter — energized by the pursuit of net-new relationships, comfortable opening doors cold, and relentless about carrying complex, multi-stakeholder deals through long sales cycles. You bring executive presence and the systems thinking to see how a single partnership fits into a broader distribution strategy. You read a term sheet and a partnership thesis with equal fluency, you make sharp prioritization calls about where to spend your time, and you carry deals with a sense of ownership. Above all, you are a builder: you're drawn to the ambiguity of standing up new channels from scratch, and you bring structure, pace, and judgment to a function that is still writing its own playbook.

About the team

The Partnerships organization is the engine behind Human Interest's reach, with over 95% of our business coming from our partner ecosystem. This team builds the relationships that let us scale access to retirement benefits far faster than we could one employer at a time. They think in systems and incentives: which partners share our mission, how we make those partners successful, and how we design programs that compound over time.

The team works shoulder-to-shoulder with Sales, Product, Marketing, Legal, and Operations to establish and launch partnerships that are commercially sound, operationally clean, and genuinely good for the businesses we ultimately serve. As we continue to scale, we're looking for a leader who can take this function to its next level: bigger partners, deeper integrations, and a measurable line on the revenue plan.

What you get to do every day

  • Team Leadership & Mentorship: Coach, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of partnership professionals, fostering a culture of ownership, strategic thinking, and high-quality deal execution.
  • Strategic Organizational Scaling: Design and implement scalable partnership processes, playbooks, and systems that allow the team to efficiently manage growth and long-term partner success.
  • Partnership Strategy: Shape and own the strategy for your portfolio of partnerships, prioritizing the channels, partner types, and deals that drive the highest-quality growth, in close partnership with the VP of Partnerships.
  • Sourcing & Closing: Act as a primary “hunter” for the organization; while guiding the team, you will remain hands-on in identifying, pursuing, and opening net-new strategic partnerships across payroll, benefits brokers, and financial institutions, personally leading high-stakes negotiations to close complex deals.
  • Performance Management: Set clear performance metrics and KPIs for the team, tracking progress and providing regular feedback to ensure the team consistently meets and exceeds revenue targets.
  • Deal Structuring & Execution: Lead commercial negotiation and deal structuring end-to-end, while empowering team members to lead negotiations on key accounts. Partner with Legal and Finance to protect the business.
  • Cross-Functional Influence: Partner with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Legal, and Sales to scope integrations, build co-marketing enablement, and operationalize partner-sourced demand.
  • Executive Communication: Translate the partnership thesis, pipeline, and results into clear narratives for the VP of Partnerships and senior leadership, and represent Human Interest externally with senior partner stakeholders.
  • Market Intelligence: Maintain a sharp view of the retirement, payroll, fintech, and benefits landscape, surfacing competitive and regulatory shifts that should shape the partnership roadmap.

What you bring to the role

  • Partnerships & Business Development Expertise: 10+ years in partnerships, business development, or channel sales, with a track record of personally owning and growing a book of strategic partnerships.
  • Leadership Experience: 5+ years experience building, coaching, and scaling high-performing teams, with a track record of enabling others to achieve revenue targets.
  • Proven Dealmaking: Demonstrated history of sourcing, structuring, and closing complex, high-value partnership and distribution agreements with measurable revenue impact.
  • Domain Fluency: Deep experience in fintech, retirement / wealth, payroll, benefits, or an adjacent financial-services ecosystem, with a working understanding of how these distribution channels actually buy and sell.
  • Cross-Functional Influence: A proven ability to mobilize Product, Engineering, Marketing, Legal, and Sales around a partnership without direct authority over those teams.
  • Executive Presence: Ability to negotiate with and present to senior executives, both internally and across partner organizations, with confidence and credibility.
  • Builder's Mindset: Thrives in a fast-paced, scaling environment; brings structure to ambiguity and is energized by standing up new motions from scratch.
  • Analytical Rigor: Strong commercial and financial instincts: able to model channel economics and make sharp prioritization calls about where to invest.
  • Values-Driven: A deep alignment with Human Interest's core principles, especially Customer Obsession, Long-Term Orientation, and Leading with Autonomy.
  • Strategic Organizational Scaling: Ability to design and operationalize partnership processes that scale beyond a single contributor, ensuring consistent growth and partner success.

Why you will love working at Human Interest

Human Interest is tackling one of our country's biggest challenges - closing the retirement gap. You'll be instrumental in architecting and scaling solutions that bring financial security to employees at small and medium-sized businesses nationwide. We’ve made significant progress, but there is still growth ahead, offering you a unique opportunity to solve complex problems, drive innovation, and advance your career alongside a dedicated, mission-driven team. We value hard work and recognize that our team's contributions are key to our continued success.

Join Human Interest and make a lasting impact by shaping the future of retirement.

Our operating principles define how we work together as a team. They reflect Human Interest’s unique view on what’s important and what’s right. Documenting this core aspect of our culture helps employees make good decisions on their own. It also helps candidates considering career opportunities critically evaluate whether they will thrive at Human Interest.

  • Customer obsession: We're all about creating amazing experiences for our customers. We put their needs first and go the extra mile to make them smile.
  • Long-Term Orientation: We're not just playing for today; we're building a legacy. We think big, plan strategically, and invest in our future.
  • Autonomous and Accountable Teams: We trust our team members to take ownership and make smart decisions. We empower you to be your best self!
  • An Escalating Bar for Talent and Performance: We're constantly raising the bar and challenging ourselves to be better. We believe in growth and continuous improvement.
  • Fundamental Optimism: We see the glass as half full (and then we fill it up with more amazing ideas!). We believe in the power of positivity and the potential for greatness.

The Role

Unraid gives people a tremendous amount of freedom to build a server around their own hardware, needs, and imagination. That flexibility is a big part of what makes the product special. It also means our Support team encounters an unusually wide range of systems, configurations, and problems.

We are hiring a Technical Support Specialist II to help users work through the more complicated end of those problems.

You will work directly with users through our general support queue and take escalations from other members of the Support team. The issues you encounter will involve storage, Linux, Docker, virtual machines, networking, hardware compatibility, plugins, third-party applications, or several of those things at once.

This is not a role where you follow a script and hand off anything unfamiliar. We have established tools, documentation, and practices, but we need someone who can investigate edge cases, connect information across different parts of a system, and make good decisions when the answer is not immediately obvious.

You will not be expected to know everything. You will be expected to know how to investigate, communicate clearly while you do it, recognize when you need another perspective, and stay connected to the person experiencing the issue until there is a responsible path forward.

This work matters. People often contact Support after they have already spent hours trying to solve a problem themselves. Sometimes the system in question holds years of personal data, family photos, creative work, or something else they cannot easily replace. A technically correct answer is important, but so are judgment, empathy, clarity, and follow-through.

What Success Looks Like

You are doing well in this role when:

  • You independently resolve a wide range of moderately complex issues across the Unraid ecosystem.
  • You can work effectively in the general support queue while also taking ownership of escalated and high-priority cases.
  • Your troubleshooting is methodical, technically sound, and clearly documented.
  • You can tell the difference between an Unraid issue and a problem involving hardware, configuration, networking, or a third-party application.
  • You keep users informed while you investigate instead of disappearing until you have a complete answer.
  • When Engineering needs to get involved, you give them the information they need to make meaningful progress.
  • You explain technical information in a way that meets people where they are.
  • You notice recurring issues and help turn what you learn into better documentation, workflows, tools, or product feedback.
  • Your public responses are useful not only to the person who asked the question, but also to the next person who finds that conversation months later.
  • You share what you know and help less-experienced teammates develop their own technical judgment.

What You’ll Do

Help Users Solve Complex Problems

  • Work directly with users through our general support queue.
  • Take escalations involving more complex or unusual technical issues.
  • Diagnose problems involving Unraid OS, arrays and pools, Linux, Docker containers, virtual machines, networking, hardware, plugins, and third-party applications.
  • Review system diagnostics, logs, configurations, and reported behavior to determine what is happening and what should happen next.
  • Troubleshoot edge cases that require you to draw on more than one established process or area of technical knowledge.
  • Help users understand what you are recommending, why you are recommending it, and any risks or tradeoffs they should consider.
  • Recognize when a case needs deeper expertise and escalate it with enough context that the next person does not have to start the investigation over.

Own Escalations Through Resolution

  • Take responsibility for high-priority cases, including issues involving data access, degraded systems, unexpected product behavior, or significant user impact.
  • Keep the user and relevant internal teams updated while the issue is being investigated.
  • Reproduce issues when practical and gather the evidence needed to determine whether a problem comes from Unraid, the user’s environment, their hardware, or a third-party component.
  • Work with Engineering, Product, and Quality when a case requires expertise or action beyond the Support team.
  • Create clear, structured bug reports that include reproduction steps, diagnostics, logs, relevant system details, expected behavior, observed behavior, and user impact.
  • Stay connected to the case when another team needs to contribute to the technical solution. Handing off part of the work does not mean handing off responsibility for the user’s experience.
  • Occasionally help outside normal working hours when a release, outage, security concern, or other urgent situation requires additional support.

Support the Unraid Community

  • Respond to technical questions in Unraid’s community spaces.
  • Write public responses with the understanding that other users may rely on them long after the original issue is resolved.
  • Help users navigate problems involving community applications and plugins while being clear about what is officially supported by Unraid and what is maintained by a third party.
  • Notice patterns in community questions and share them with Support, Product, Quality, and Engineering.
  • Help maintain a community where people with very different levels of technical knowledge can ask questions and receive useful, respectful answers.

Make Support Better

  • Document new issues, troubleshooting approaches, and confirmed solutions.
  • Update documentation when the product or our recommended guidance changes.
  • Identify recurring problems, gaps in our resources, and opportunities to prevent avoidable support volume.
  • Suggest practical improvements to our processes, tools, documentation, and product.
  • Help us test and improve AI-assisted support tools while applying your own judgment to the output.
  • Look for ways to reduce repeated work without reducing the quality or humanity of the support we provide.
  • Share what you are hearing from users so that other teams can use it to make better decisions.

Contribute to the Team

  • Share technical knowledge, resources, and lessons learned with the rest of the Support team.
  • Give and receive thoughtful, constructive feedback.
  • Help junior teammates strengthen their troubleshooting skills and make good escalation decisions.
  • Build productive relationships with people across Support, Quality, Engineering, and Product.
  • Participate in team meetings, training, reporting, and the shared work required to keep a small remote team running well.
  • Help the team move through releases, product changes, and new processes with clarity and calm.

What “Technical” Means in This Role

Unraid is a Linux-based operating system used across an enormous range of hardware, storage, networking, virtualization, and application environments. Supporting it well requires more than knowing where things are in the interface.

You should be comfortable investigating a problem across multiple layers of a system and thinking about how those layers affect one another. That includes:

  • Linux filesystems, permissions, processes, services, logs, and command-line troubleshooting
  • Unraid arrays, parity, cache and storage pools, drive behavior, and data-protection concepts
  • ZFS and other storage configurations supported within the Unraid ecosystem
  • Docker containers, including configuration, networking, volumes, permissions, and application behavior
  • Virtual machines, KVM/QEMU, hardware assignment, and common virtualization issues
  • Local networking, remote access, DNS, routing, ports, shares, and connectivity
  • Server hardware, storage devices, controllers, memory, firmware, and hardware compatibility
  • Plugins and community applications
  • System diagnostics and logs, including the ability to identify useful signals without jumping too quickly to a conclusion

No one knows everything about every possible Unraid configuration. That is not what we are looking for. We are looking for someone with strong technical foundations who knows how to investigate what they do not yet understand.

Your First 90 Days

Your first 90 days are about understanding before reshaping.

We will invest real time in helping you learn the product, the team, and the way Support operates today. We expect you to invest that time back into listening, asking questions, learning the history behind our decisions, and resisting the urge to redesign something before you understand why it exists.

During this period, you will:

  • Learn our support tools, documentation, communication standards, and escalation paths.
  • Build a deeper understanding of Unraid’s architecture, supported functionality, common problems, and current product priorities.
  • Review existing support cases and see how experienced team members investigate, communicate, and make decisions.
  • Begin working directly with users and take on increasingly complex cases as you become ready.
  • Learn how we navigate the space between official Unraid functionality and third-party applications, plugins, and hardware.
  • Build working relationships with people in Support, Quality, Engineering, Product, and other parts of the company.
  • Notice opportunities for improvement while taking the time to understand the history and consequences of changing the current approach.

By the end of the introductory period, you should be independently resolving a meaningful range of cases, contributing useful documentation, and showing good judgment about when to keep investigating and when to bring in additional expertise.

What We’re Looking For

  • Around three or more years of experience in technical support, systems administration, infrastructure support, or another role where you regularly diagnosed complex technical problems
  • Meaningful hands-on experience using and administering Unraid
  • Strong working knowledge of Linux and comfort using the command line, logs, and system diagnostics to investigate problems
  • Experience troubleshooting storage systems, filesystems, hardware, networking, Docker containers, and virtual machines
  • The ability to isolate a problem across interconnected systems
  • Experience owning technical cases through resolution instead of simply identifying and transferring them
  • Good judgment about when to continue investigating, when to ask for another perspective, and when to escalate
  • The ability to explain technical information clearly to people with different levels of knowledge
  • A methodical approach to documenting investigations, findings, and next steps
  • Strong organization and follow-through across multiple active cases
  • The ability to work well with other people when the situation is complicated, urgent, or frustrating
  • A genuine interest in helping people—not just solving machines

We care more about what you can do than how you learned to do it. A specific degree or certification is not required. Professional experience, independent technical work, community contributions, and demonstrated Unraid expertise may all be relevant.

Nice to Have

  • Experience supporting a Linux-based software product
  • Experience with NAS, homelab, self-hosting, or server infrastructure
  • Experience troubleshooting ZFS, virtualization, GPU passthrough, or containerized applications
  • Experience supporting customer-owned hardware or other environments where configurations vary widely
  • Experience turning technical investigations into useful bug reports for Engineering
  • Experience contributing to technical forums, community support, or public knowledge bases
  • Experience writing or maintaining technical documentation
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted support, search, triage, or knowledge-management tools
  • Experience working with a SaaS, open-source, developer-focused, or technically engaged user community
  • Comfort working in a small company where responsibilities sometimes cross traditional boundaries

Growth & Opportunity

We have career paths for people who want to deepen their technical expertise and for people who may eventually want to lead others. Management is not the only way to grow here.

From this role, you may grow into Technical Support Specialist III by developing deeper knowledge of Unraid’s architecture, taking on more ambiguous and high-impact problems, working more closely with Engineering and Product, and leading improvements to our tools, documentation, or training.

Depending on your strengths, interests, and the needs of the company, other paths may develop in support engineering, quality, documentation, technical education, product, or people management.

We do not promise that every path will be immediately available. We do commit to talking openly about where you want to grow, helping you understand what the next level requires, and looking for meaningful opportunities to develop along the way.

You’re the Right Fit If…

  • You can work independently with general direction and know when to ask for help.
  • You like investigating technical problems, especially when the first explanation does not hold up.
  • You take responsibility for the user’s experience, not just the technical task in front of you.
  • You can be technically direct without making someone feel small for not knowing what you know.
  • You are comfortable saying, “I don’t know yet,” and then doing the work to find out.
  • You communicate proactively instead of leaving users or teammates wondering what is happening.
  • You understand that closing a ticket quickly is not always the same as resolving it well.
  • You can work typical office hours of 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. in your local time zone within UTC -5 to UTC -10.
  • You can occasionally help outside normal working hours when an urgent, high-impact situation requires it.
  • You have experience working remotely and can manage your time, priorities, and communication without close supervision.
  • You can join us in person for two week-long annual staff offsites, held in the spring and fall. Some are within the United States and others are international.
  • You like being part of a small team and are comfortable picking up work that may not fit neatly inside a job description.
  • You communicate clearly and thoughtfully in writing and conversation.

Pay & Benefits

Compensation & Retirement

  • Annual salary of 70,000–90,000, based on experience and alignment with the role
  • Annual raise
  • Annual bonus*
  • Annual profit sharing*
  • Up to 6% 401(k) match

Health & Wellness

  • 100% medical coverage for employees and 50% coverage for dependents
  • 100% dental and vision coverage for employees and dependents
  • Annual employee wellness budget*

Time Off & Leave

  • 30 full days and 14 half days of Flexible Time Off,* plus 11 paid holidays
  • Paid parental leave for the birth, adoption, or placement of a child, available after one year of employment

Professional Development & Support

  • Free access to a team mentor
  • Reimbursement for online or in-person professional development
  • Annual home office budget*
  • Annual spring and fall staff offsites

*Available after completion of the 90-day introductory period.

About Our Team & Culture

We put people first. We are bringing together a team of people who are exceptional in their areas of work, work well together, and have the trust and support they need to do their best work.

We are fully remote and have been since Day 1. That requires us to communicate clearly, follow through on what we say we will do, and trust one another to manage our work. We value thoughtful disagreement, direct communication, and an environment where people can ask questions or admit mistakes without being punished for it.

We care about how work gets done, not just what gets finished. We regularly review our systems and meeting cadence to keep our operations useful and straightforward. We would rather spend our time making the product and experience better than sorting through endless emails or sitting through meetings that did not need to happen.

We also do not take ourselves too seriously. Unraid has always been a little rebellious: flexible where other products are rigid, practical where the industry tends to overcomplicate things, and built for people who want more control over their own hardware. That spirit still shows up in how we work—and sometimes in an unreasonable number of Hawaiian shirts.

You can learn more about our history and leadership by watchingthis Uncast interview and exploring ourAbout page andTeam page.

About Lime Technology, Inc.

Lime Technology is the company behind Unraid OS. Founded in 2005 and headquartered in San Diego, California, we are a family-owned company with employees across the United States and contractors around the world.

Unraid helps people get more out of their hardware. Our users build systems to store and protect their data, host media, run applications, create virtual machines, and do plenty of things we never would have thought to prescribe for them.

Built on a proprietary Linux-based operating system, Unraid allows users to combine drives of different types and sizes within a parity-protected array. It also provides a flexible platform for Docker applications and virtual machines using technologies including KVM, QEMU, and GPU passthrough.

Unraid is shaped by a deeply knowledgeable and engaged community. Hundreds of user-contributed applications, tools, and plugins extend what the product can do. That community is one of the best things about Unraid—and supporting it well requires technical depth, humility, curiosity, and a real willingness to help.

Join us in helping people Unleash Their Hardware.

jobs.description:
CEO Advisor | Help Business Owners Grow | $182K+ OTE | Remote

How To MANAGE a Small Law Firm (HTM)

Location: 100% remote. You must live in one of these 14 states: AZ, CO, FL, GA, IL, MD, MI, NC, NJ, NY, PA, TX, VA, or WA. Applications from other states cannot be considered.

Compensation: $110,000 base salary + performance compensation | $182,000+ total earnings potential

Employment: Full-time W-2 employee (not a fractional, contract, or side role)

You've run a business, and you've helped other owners run theirs. Now do it every day, with clients we bring you.

Most attorneys who own a law firm were trained to practice law, not to run a business. They're great lawyers dealing with cash flow, pricing, hiring, and growth, often without anyone in their corner who has been there.

As a CEO Advisor at HTM, you'll work one-on-one with small and midsized law firm owners. You'll help them build a business plan, understand their numbers, make the hard calls, and follow through. You don't need a legal background. You need to have owned a business's results yourself and have a track record of helping other owners get results.

We bring you the clients. You bring the experience.

What you'll do

  • Meet regularly with law firm owners to set growth targets, establish priorities, and build an actionable business plan.
  • Review revenue, expenses, margins, and cash flow to identify opportunities to improve profitability.
  • Help owners solve operational problems involving staffing, workflow, intake, pricing, and systems.
  • Challenge assumptions, coach owners through difficult decisions, and hold them accountable for following through.
  • Help owners build firms that operate more effectively without depending on them for every decision and that increase in value over time.

Who we're looking for

  • You've advised small business owners. You have a track record of working one-on-one with owners of small and midsized businesses on strategy, financial performance, and growth as an advisor, coach, consultant, fractional executive, or peer-group leader.
  • You've owned the P&L. You've been an owner, CEO, or President with company-wide P&L responsibility, accountable for the financial performance and overall success of the business—not just one department, business unit, or location.
  • You've operated at the right scale. You've run a business with annual revenue between approximately $500K and $30M, and you can explain the decisions that drove its results.
  • You can point to results. You can describe specific owners you've helped and business decisions you've made, along with what changed in revenue, profit, or cash flow.
  • You understand how the money works. You know how pricing, margins, cash flow, people, and operations connect to profitability and business growth.
  • You're direct and you follow through. You're comfortable telling an owner what they need to hear, helping them make difficult decisions, and holding them accountable until the plan is carried out.
  • Bonus: Experience with professional-services firms (legal, accounting, medical, engineering, or consulting), either running one or advising their owners.

This role is probably not a fit if:

  • You haven't held company-wide P&L responsibility as an owner, CEO, or President.
  • Your experience is primarily in large corporations or in a single functional area, such as sales, procurement, marketing, operations administration, or engineering.
  • You haven't worked one-on-one with small business owners as an advisor or coach.
  • You live outside the 14 eligible states listed above.
  • You want to continue running your own practice or another business alongside this role.

Compensation and benefits

  • $110,000 base salary.
  • $182,000+ total earnings potential through performance-based compensation.
  • Uncapped performance opportunity, subject to the terms of the compensation plan.
  • HTM's Elite Benefits Bundle.
  • Full-time W-2 employment, with clients provided by HTM.

How to apply

Click Apply and complete the short questionnaire. Applications without completed answers won't be reviewed.
