jobs.description:
Berry Street is on a mission to transform how Americans eat through nutrition therapy. Berry Street’s platform connects individuals needing evidence-based nutrition care with an expansive network of Registered Dietitians and AI-powered tools. From weight management, diabetes, and heart health to kidney disease, maternal health, and 25+ other conditions, Berry Street’s clinical team delivers personalized nutrition interventions tailored to each patient's unique physiological and psychological needs, improving outcomes and reducing total cost of care. Berry Street works with some of the largest health plans, as well as leading health systems and innovative care management companies to serve diverse populations across all 50 states.

Since launching in January 2023, Berry Street has grown to over 1,500 providers and served tens of thousands of patients nationwide. We’re a Series B company backed by leadin investors including Northzone, Sofina, and FJ Labs, and notable angels including the founders of Revolut, Spring Health and Grow Therapy.

The Role

Berry Street is expanding into GLP-1 prescribing and is seeking board-certified Physicians (MD or DO) to join our independent contractor prescriber network. You will provide telehealth clinical evaluations, prescribe and titrate GLP-1 medications for weight management patients, and collaborate with our RD team - all fully remote, on a schedule you control.

What You'll Do

  • Conduct synchronous telehealth evaluations for new GLP-1 patients, assessing eligibility, comorbidities, contraindications, and treatment goals per Berry Street’s clinical protocol
  • Prescribe and titrate FDA-approved GLP-1 medications (Wegovy, Zepbound, Ozempic, Mounjaro, etc.)
  • Manage and supervise follow-up visits, dose titration, side effect counseling, and lab review through a mix of synchronous visits and async chart review, per applicable state law
  • Review Berry Street RD care summaries before prescribing encounters and reference documented lifestyle modification history in your clinical documentation
  • Sign Letters of Medical Necessity for prior authorization submissions; PA Coordinators handle all ePA logistics and submissions
  • Respond to PA appeals requiring clinical input within 48 hours and support renewal PA documentation every 6-12 months
  • Participate in Medical Director-led clinical reviews, protocol updates, and quality improvement initiatives to continuously refine the prescribing experience
  • Practice within Berry Street’s Professional Corporation (PC) in full CPOM compliance — all clinical decisions are entirely yours
  • Maintain active licensure, malpractice coverage, and payer credentialing across contracted states
  • Participate in periodic chart audits and quality reviews led by the Medical Director

Requirements

  • MD or DO from an accredited U.S. medical school; board-certified in Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Emergency Medicine, or a related specialty (ABMS or AOA)
  • Active, unrestricted medical licenses in a minimum of 30 U.S. states; willingness to obtain additional licenses to support patient footprint strongly preferred; IMLC enrollment or eligibility is a significant plus
  • Minimum 3 years of post-residency clinical experience managing patients with obesity, metabolic syndrome, or type 2 diabetes
  • Comfort practicing in a fully remote clinical environment with proficiency in EHR platforms
  • Active NPI and professional liability / malpractice insurance covering telehealth encounters
  • Board certification or training in Obesity Medicine (ABOM) is a plus
  • Prior telehealth prescribing experience in weight management or metabolic health is a plus
  • Licenses in high-volume states (CA, TX, FL, NY, PA, IL, OH, GA, NC, AZ) are a significant plus

Benefits

  • Total schedule flexibility - set your own hours with a minimum of 10 hours of recurring patient-facing availability per week.
  • Hourly fee structure - competitive with top telehealth GLP-1 platforms; specific rate shared during interview process.
  • Guaranteed hours - we guarantee pay for every hour of availability you set in our EHR (Healthie).
  • Limited administrative overhead - PA Coordinators, MSO billing, and scheduling are handled for you.
  • Best-in-class PA documentation - Berry Street’s existing RD records mean higher PA approval rates.
  • Integrated clinical support - RD team manages nutrition, GI side effects, and behavioral change, reducing your burden.

jobs.excerpt: About UsWork a four-day week from anywhere for a company where people genuinely believe in what they do.
jobs.description:
About Us

Work a four-day week from anywhere for a company where people genuinely believe in what they do. Wonderlic leads the way in fair, predictive science to create a world where everyone finds and thrives in their best job—and that starts with you. We expertly combine our science-based assessment expertise with I-O psychology, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to deliver evidence-based insights that empower smarter employment decisions. Our simple, intuitive assessment tools help sophisticated HR teams identify top applicants, predict on-the-job performance, and ensure our own team is engaged and equipped to do their best work.

Wonderlic has always championed progressive, sustainable approaches that allow people to excel professionally while living balanced, fulfilling lives.Here are some of the ways we do that: 

  • Work from anywhere in the United States 
  • Four-day work week
  • Generous PTO plus a paid company shutdown from 12/24 to 1/1
  • Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k with matching, paid new parent leave

What Sets Us Apart:

  • Scientific Precision: We apply rigorous scientific methodologies to develop assessments that accurately gauge individuals' potential and fit within various organizational contexts.
  • Innovation: Our dedication to continuous improvement drives us to explore cutting-edge techniques and technologies, ensuring our assessments remain at the forefront of talent assessment.
  • Impactful Solutions: By integrating I-O Psychology principles into our processes, we deliver solutions that not only meet the immediate hiring needs of organizations but also contribute to long-term success and retention.

Overview:

Wonderlic is seeking a Senior Research Scientist to sit at the precise intersection of I-O psychology and machine learning - someone who has spent time building real systems with real data who cares deeply about what those systems are predicting. This is not a role for an ML engineer who finds people data interesting as a side project, or for an I-O psychologist who has learned to code. We’re looking for someone who has genuinely lived in both worlds and is ready to own the problems that live between them.

Wonderlic built its applied AI/ML team from scratch, developed the Jobs Engine, a first-of-its-kind machine learning system for job analysis at scale, and won the 2025 SIOP Machine Learning Competition. We’re now refining and expanding that work to deliver sharper, richer job analysis insights across thousands of roles. You will own the continued improvement of our jobs engine, the system that ingests labor market data and produces job analysis at scale across thousands of roles, and serve as one of the organization’s experts on how AI should be applied to both employee selection and development.

Your Impact:

As Senior Research Scientist, you will set the scientific and technical direction for how Wonderlic understands work at scale and translates assessment science into AI-powered insight. Your work will directly determine the quality, defensibility, and reach of the inferences our platform makes about jobs and people - inferences that drive hiring decisions, development plans, and coaching conversations for millions of users. You will be the person in the organization who can hold both the I-O science question and the production ML question in the same breath, and answer both.

What You’ll Do

Lead the Continued Development of the Jobs Engine: Own the architecture, integrity, and continuous expansion of Wonderlic’s AI job analysis system, which ingests labor market data from O*NET, LinkedIn, Indeed, and other sources to extrapolate cognitive complexity ratings, norm groups, and occupational interest profiles for thousands of jobs. Build and refine the models that make inferences about work content from unstructured text. Leverage existing occupational taxonomies (e.g., O*NET, ESCO) where appropriate but also expand beyond them. Ensure all outputs are scientifically defensible and scalable as the nature of work evolves.

Act as an Expert on AI Implementation Across the Organization: Partner with product managers, engineers, and I-O psychologists to translate scientific requirements into AI-powered systems and ensure those systems meet the standards the work demands. Advise on which approaches are best suited to specific implementation challenges - assessment interpretation, manager and teams reporting, coaching content - and help teams understand what good looks like before they build and after they ship. Serve as an internal resource on what ML and AI can and cannot do in assessment and organizational contexts, and contribute to Wonderlic’s external scientific credibility.

Drive Scientific Rigor: Apply I-O psychology principles - adverse impact consideration, norm group construction, and evidence-based evaluation standards - to every system you build. Ensure that Wonderlic’s AI products meet professional and legal standards for selection and development tools. Push back when speed is being prioritized at the expense of defensibility, and find pragmatic paths forward when theoretical purity would prevent shipping.

What Success Looks Like: In your first six months, you will have a deep understanding of the jobs engine architecture and shipped at least one meaningful improvement to its coverage, accuracy, or scientific defensibility. You will have established working
relationships with the I-O and Product teams and have a clear roadmap for the continued integration of AI into the platform.

Within a year, you will have materially expanded the jobs engine’s reach and accuracy with demonstrable improvements to its coverage and the quality of inferences it produces. You will have contributed to the continued integration of AI across the platform, and be the person your colleagues go to with the hardest ML-meets-IO-science problems - not because you have every answer, but because you know how to find them.

The long-term marker of success is a jobs engine that provides defensible, scaled job analysis inference across millions of roles using a wide variety of inputs, AI capabilities integrated into the platform in ways that hold up to scientific and professional scrutiny, and a track record of using these technologies to improve people’s understanding of themselves, their work, and their teams. You will also have helped to develop new assessments that leverage emerging technologies which allow for richer and more secure evaluation of individuals.

What We’re Looking For:

Skills & Capabilities:

  • Applied NLP and ML engineering skills: embeddings, semantic search, clustering, text classification, transformer architectures, model tuning and evaluation, all on potentially messy, unstructured data
  • Occupational data modeling: job titles, task statements, skills, competencies, credentials, job families, seniority levels, title normalization, job similarity, role differentiation, and occupational frameworks such as O*NET and ESCO
  • Responsible AI judgment in employment contexts: fairness, explainability, auditability, bias mitigation, human review, and legal and ethical considerations in AI-supported selection and employee development systems
  • Generative AI evaluation skills: rubric-based review, groundedness checks, error analysis, regression testing, and evaluation of LLM-generated job descriptions, work-context summaries, and assessment result contextualization.
  • Product judgment for applied ML systems: balancing accuracy, explainability, automation, expert review, user input, maintainability, uncertainty, and job-specific nuance.
  • Working fluency with assessment and I/O concepts: job relatedness, criterion relationships, adverse impact, norm groups, assessment profiles, and score interpretation.
  • Ability to own ambiguous, high-complexity problems: framing underspecified problems, challenging weak assumptions, learning domain constraints quickly, and driving durable solutions in a small-company environment.

Mindset:

  • You came to I-O psychology because you care about work - what makes it meaningful, who thrives in it, how to measure fit. That hasn’t changed.
  • You have a healthy relationship with “good enough”: you know that perfect is the enemy of shipped, and you have the judgment to know where the line is.
  • You can hold both worlds simultaneously: what does this score mean for a real person, and how do I build the system that generates it.
  • You are genuinely curious about the problems that exist for both employee selection and development, not just tolerant of them.
  • You thrive in an environment that requires creativity and scrappiness: you can work comfortably in a situation where the problems are hard, the team is small, the constraints are many, and the ownership is real.

Qualifications

  • Graduate degree in I-O Psychology, Organizational Psychology, Organizational Development, or closely related field (quantitative focus strongly preferred); doctoral degree a plus
  • Demonstrated ML engineering experience with shipped, production-grade systems - not just research or coursework
  • Experience applying modern NLP methods to behavioral, assessment-based, or labor market data
  • Track record of work that had to be both technically sound and legally/professionally defensible
  • Minimum 3 years of applied industry experience; 5+ years preferred
  • Experience at the intersection of I-O science and algorithmic fairness strongly preferred
  • Familiarity with occupational taxonomies, vocational interests, or cognitive ability frameworks a significant plus

Compensation:

  • $130,000 to $150,000 based on experience and expertise.

Our Policy

Affirmative Action Plan/Equal Employer Opportunity (AAP/EEO) Statement: Research suggests that both the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can make members of some groups (including women, members of the LGBTQIA+ and BIPOC communities, and candidates of less traditional age, education, or background) less likely to apply for jobs when they don’t meet 100% of the qualifications. At Wonderlic, we are in the business of identifying potential, and we encourage all interested candidates to apply. 

Wonderlic is proud to be an equal employment opportunity/affirmative action employer. Here, diversity is valued and celebrated, and this is what makes us such a successful team. Wonderlic does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, pregnancy status, national origin, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, genetic information, age, parental status, military/veteran status, or any other factor protected by law.

In addition, we will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please get in touch with us at  to request an accommodation.

About Sharing Excess

Sharing Excess is one of the fastest-growing food rescue organizations in America, built on a simple but powerful mission: save food and feed communities. What started as a student startup now operates hubs in Philadelphia, New York (Hunts Point), Chicago, and Detroit, redistributing surplus food at scale to reduce waste and close the meal gap.

Our work is fast-paced, human-centered, and deeply mission-driven. We move quickly, adapt constantly, and build systems that allow compassion to scale. We are looking for team members who bring both heart and rigor to their work and want to help build a strong, values-aligned organization from the inside out.

Role Overview

The HR Generalist, Recruiting owns hiring at Sharing Excess. You will run full-cycle recruitment across every hub and department, from warehouse and driver roles to program leadership, and make sure every candidate experiences our values from first contact to first day.

Recruiting is roughly 70% of this role. The other 30% is generalist work: you are a trained backup on core HR operations and step in when the team needs coverage, including onboarding, employee questions, HRIS updates, and compliance tasks. This is a role for a recruiter who wants to grow as an HR generalist, or a generalist who loves the hiring side of the work.

You will be part of a small, hands-on HR team led by the HR Manager and will partner closely with the Senior HR Generalist, Compliance & Payroll so hiring and onboarding hand off cleanly.

Core Responsibilities

Full-Cycle Recruitment (approx. 70%)

  • Own the hiring process end to end: intake meetings, job postings, sourcing, screening, interview scheduling, debriefs, references, and offers
  • Partner with hiring managers to define role needs, interview plans, and selection criteria before a role opens
  • Source candidates proactively through job boards, community partners, workforce programs, colleges, and referrals, with a focus on local talent in each hub
  • Manage high-volume hourly hiring for warehouse, driver, and operations roles alongside professional and leadership searches
  • Coach managers on structured, inclusive, and legally compliant interviewing
  • Maintain the applicant tracking system and keep candidates informed at every stage
  • Prepare offer letters in partnership with the HR Manager and hand new hires off smoothly to onboarding
  • Track and report recruiting metrics, including time to fill, pipeline health, source of hire, and offer acceptance
  • Keep the careers page and job postings current, and make sure our employer brand reflects our mission and culture
  • Support the annual hiring plan and keep open roles aligned with the approved hiring budget

Generalist Coverage (approx. 30%)

  • Step in as backup HR Generalist when the team needs coverage, including absences, peak periods, and special projects
  • Support new hire onboarding: paperwork, I-9 verification, orientation, and 30/60/90-day check-ins
  • Serve as a point of contact for employee HR questions and route sensitive or complex issues to the HR Manager
  • Keep employee records and HRIS data accurate
  • Assist with compliance tasks, including training tracking, postings, and audit preparation, in partnership with the Senior HR Generalist, Compliance & Payroll
  • Support offboarding, exit interviews, engagement surveys, and culture initiatives as needed

You'll Have

  • 4+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, in-house or agency
  • Experience with both high-volume hourly hiring and professional or salaried searches
  • Working knowledge of HR operations, such as onboarding, I-9s, HRIS, and employee relations basics
  • Familiarity with employment law as it applies to hiring, including fair chance and pay transparency requirements
  • Experience with an applicant tracking system and HRIS
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to build trust quickly with candidates and managers
  • Strong organization, follow-through, and discretion with confidential information
  • Willingness and ability to travel occasionally to Sharing Excess hub locations as needed

It's Great If You Also Have

  • HR Generalist experience or a PHR, SHRM-CP, or similar certification
  • Experience recruiting in multiple states, especially PA, NY, IL, or MI
  • Nonprofit, food systems, logistics, or warehouse hiring experience
  • Bilingual skills, especially Spanish

You'll Be Successful If You

  • Treat every candidate like a future colleague, whether or not they get the job
  • Push hiring forward with urgency without cutting corners
  • Stay curious about the whole employee lifecycle, from first contact through long after the hire
  • Balance structure with flexibility as priorities shift
  • Care deeply about building systems that support people

$60,000 to $75,000 per year, commensurate with experience and location.

jobs.excerpt: Job Description A bit about this role: Devoted Health’s long-term vision is to create a virtual "blue zone" for its members, where they can live longer, healthier lives by receiving the right care, in the right place, at the right time, in a proactive and coordinated way.
jobs.description:
Job Description

A bit about this role:


Devoted Health’s long-term vision is to create a virtual "blue zone" for its members, where they can live longer, healthier lives by receiving the right care, in the right place, at the right time, in a proactive and coordinated way. When the traditional/ ‘status quo’ health system fails to provide, Devoted members can rely on Devoted Medical, an innovative, world-class care delivery system whose primary directive is to treat each member like family.


Transitions of Care (TOC) is one of Devoted Medical’s largest clinical programs, responsible for ensuring that thousands of Devoted members return home safely after hospitalization. From admission through 30 days post-discharge, our highly skilled, virtual interdisciplinary teams deliver personalized and comprehensive ‘wrap around care’ to break down the gamut of clinical, social & logistical barriers to post-discharge stability. This member-centric approach has already yielded substantial, sustained reductions in post-discharge complications and readmissions, and we’re continuously evolving our care model to keep more members safe at home.


That’s where you come in. We are looking for a seasoned, conscientious, and transformational clinical leader and thought partner, a scrappy, empathetic, determined individual with a proven track record in leading high performing clinical teams. Partnering closely with TOC’s clinical & operational leaders, the Senior Manager will be accountable for a significant frontline workforce (~60-70 frontline RNs) to provide excellent interdisciplinary care in the 30-day window after patients leave the hospital. The Senior Manager will develop and inspire a team of managers to lead engaged, quality-oriented teams that obsess over caring for patients like family and help them stay healthy at home.


Required skills and experience: (4-5 bullets recommended max*)

  • 5+ years of experience leading high performing clinical teams in a transitional care and/or care management setting, ideally across a virtual and/or geographically dispersed workforce
  • 3+ years of experience in coaching and developing other leaders/managers (i.e. past manager-of-managers)
  • Active RN license in good standing, and/or BSN or equivalent related degree, master’s preferred
  • Experience in post-acute medicine, nursing and case management processes, internal medicine, urgent care, emergency room, hospital medicine, and/or geriatrics
  • Experience managing and/or working in an interdisciplinary care team setting, along with a strong conviction for interdisciplinary care in general
  • Extensive experience as an enthusiastic change agent/transformational leader

Desired skills and experience: (1-2 bullets max*)

  • Compassionate, service-oriented leader that rolls up their sleeves, shows their work, seeks feedback & builds consensus
  • Curious & collaborative operations-minded problem-solver who knows how to recognize process deficiencies, recommend improvements and implement solutions
  • Energized by a fast-paced, rapidly growing organization, with the agility, resilience, and a growth mindset to embrace change and rapid cycles of quality improvement
  • Deeply empathetic and humanistic- you develop engaged teams that have a deep culture of service to members/patients
  • Excellent communication skills, someone who thoughtfully adapts their style based on audience and nature of the message in both written and verbal contexts
  • Certification in Case Management a plus!

Your Responsibilities and Impact will include: (6-7 bullets max recommended*)

  • Transformational Clinician Leadership: Cultivate & inspire a collaborative, patient-oriented, high-performing team of front-line nurses, care coordinators, educators & nurse leaders dedicated to improving post-acute patient experiences & outcomes
  • Coaching & Development: Drive hiring, training, workflow improvement, skill development, and performance management strategies for frontline teams and managers
  • Results-Driven Performance Management: Track & manage staff performance against a combination of productivity, quality of care and clinical outcome KPIs to ultimately reduce avoidable admissions & readmissions; lead regular meetings with managers & front-line staff to provide feedback, identify & act upon opportunities for improvement, and provide consistent coaching & encouragement
  • Servant Leadership: This individual will be expected to provide frontline patient care 10% -20% of their week; we consider this work essential in developing a deep understanding of how our program works and where we can improve, and in building lasting trust/followership among the frontline and management team
  • Thought Partnership: Work closely with other clinical & operational program leads to shape the program’s scope, strategy & execution to optimize outcomes for our patients & our interdisciplinary care teams

Salary range: $110,000 - $173,000 annually

The pay range listed for this position is the range the organization reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for this position at the time of the posting. Once the interview process begins, your talent partner will provide additional information on the compensation for the role, along with additional information on our total rewards package. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job.

Our Total Rewards package includes:

  • Employer sponsored health, dental and vision plan with low or no premium

  • Generous paid time off

  • $100 monthly mobile or internet stipend

  • Stock options for all employees

  • Bonus eligibility for all roles excluding Director and above; Commission eligibility for Sales roles

  • Parental leave program

  • 401K program

  • And more....

*Our total rewards package is for full time employees only. Intern and Contract positions are not eligible.

Founded in 2017, Devoted Health is on a mission to dramatically improve the health and well-being of older Americans by caring for everyone like they are family, and that includes our employees. Our robust and seamlessly integrated care platform merges advanced data and AI access with world-class clinical and service experiences to create a member experience that is unlike the industry norm. To continue building upon our mission, we want to bring together those who share our values, embrace change and advancement, and are enthusiastic about where we're going — all the while bringing their own unique qualities, experiences, and expertise, in hopes of further changing the healthcare experience.


Devoted is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to a safe and supportive work environment in which all employees have the opportunity to participate and contribute to the success of the business. We value diversity and collaboration. Individuals are respected for their skills, experience, and unique perspectives. This commitment is embodied in Devoted’s Code of Conduct, our company values and the way we do business.


As an Equal Opportunity Employer, the Company does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy status, marital status, national origin, disability, age, sexual orientation, veteran status, genetic information, gender identity, gender expression, or any other factor prohibited by law. Our management team is dedicated to this policy with respect to recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, transfer, training, compensation, benefits, employee activities and general treatment during employment.

jobs.description:
How You’ll Contribute

The Advancement team identifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards individuals, as well as foundation, government, and corporate partners who invest in the Society to drive impact through science, technology, education, exploration, and storytelling. The team collaborates across the Society – and often works closely with NGP/Disney – to build transformative and impact-driven strategic partnerships. The team also produces global events that deepen connections and leverage the Society’s power to convene, and directs robust annual, major, and planned giving programs empowering the Society with a broad base of public support.

The Annual Giving and Membership (AGM) team manages a high impact fundraising and stewardship program through integrated and data-driven marketing and communications campaigns across multiple channels. The Senior Manager, Digital Fundraising is responsible for managing the digital fundraising program for the Advancement team to meet growing revenue goals for the National Geographic Society across mobile, email, web, digital ads, and other digital channels to acquire, retain, and reactivate donors at both the membership level and mid-level, while helping to steward and inspire current donors.

Your Impact

Responsibilities Include


Lead and Manage Robust and Innovative Digital Fundraising Program – 50%

  • Project manage all aspects of the digital fundraising program in support of lead generation, acquisition, retention, and reactivation goals in collaboration with internal and external partners to meet long- and short-term targets.
  • Lead the development of a full-scale text-to-give fundraising program.
  • Serve as lead digital fundraising liaison with internal enterprise-wide partners (such as Communications, IT, and Strategic Insights, among others) as well with NGP’s digital, social, marketing teams, etc. and with external vendors to develop, implement, and optimize digital campaigns that promote donor acquisition and engagement in support of increasing revenue goals.
  • Serve as a partner to internal teams in developing strategic digital plans for the Society that optimize fundraising and stewardship in support of overall donor and revenue goals.
  • Collaborate with AGM channel and program leads to create and implement the annual digital calendar and strategies to establish a regular cadence of member communication and a robust plan for digital acquisition using display advertising, email, SMS, third-party promotions, paid search, e-appends, and other types of digital acquisition.
  • Lead internal and external partners in the development of integrated digital campaign materials, writing and designing content as needed.
  • Lead the alignment and integration of digital strategies and tactics with print and other direct marketing campaigns in collaboration with the larger AGM team as well as throughout the Advancement department.
  • Collaborate with the NGS Communications and marketing team to ensure fundraising appeals are aligned with Society priorities and brand requirements.
  • Research and build expertise of current and emerging fundraising technologies across all aspects of digital fundraising/marketing and make recommendations for program innovations.

Create and Implement Online Stewardship and Cultivation Plans – 25%

  • In collaboration with AGM channel and program leads, support the execution of online stewardship and cultivation plans for donors and subscribers, including broad engagement emails and text broadcasts, personalized mid-level communications, integrated and interest-driven e-newsletters, automated email/SMS ladders, special announcements, etc. to recognize donors, communicate gratitude, and demonstrate impact of donations.
  • Manage the development and execution of integrated donor journeys to build a pipeline of giving that stewards, retains and upgrades supporters.
  • Manage the execution of digital engagement campaigns and broadcasts in support of other Advancement teams for other donor and VIP audiences as needed.
  • Research and propose innovations in digital stewardship to continually innovate and improve communications that deepen engagement with NGS’s mission.

Manage Program Analysis and Digital Testing Plan– 10%

  • Analyze effectiveness of digital fundraising campaigns and digital presence and help establish NGS benchmarks and compare performance to industry benchmarks.
  • Monitor and interpret program KPIs, revenue and engagement data, trends, successes, and outcomes and share timely, proactive, and ongoing results and insights with team and other key colleagues.
  • Manage testing plan and roadmap to optimize digital fundraising program and meet revenue, engagement, and other goals.
  • Oversee tracking and reconciliation of gifts between systems in collaboration with Gift Processing to ensure data is accurate and donor intent is followed.

Manage Digital Fundraising Collateral and Digital Donation Experience – 10%

  • Oversee regular audits of digital fundraising collateral to ensure evergreen content is continually monitored and refreshed to ensure the best digital user experience.
  • Oversee, update and optimize the Society’s digital acquisition and opt-in landing pages including recommending and implementing continual upgrades and innovations.
  • Partner with Advancement Operations and external vendors to ensure the digital fundraising program is effectively, efficiently, and creatively utilizing both existing and new functionality to continually enhance and improve user experience.

Perform other duties as assigned - 5%.


What You’ll Bring


Educational Background

Bachelor’s degree preferred.


Minimum Years and Type of Experience

7+ years digital marketing/fundraising experience with demonstrated expertise on current and emerging trends in digital fundraising and constituent engagement.


Necessary Knowledge and Skills

  • Proven donor/member strategy and communications skills, including experience in creating effective digital fundraising and omnichannel campaigns.
  • Experience managing and scaling text-to-give fundraising programs.
  • Innovative and willing to take risks while maintaining focus on protecting the brand.
  • Excellent strategist able to leverage data to increase results.
  • Creative and outstanding fundraising writer and content developer for mobile, email, website, digital ads, and/or social media.
  • Strong project management skills. Must be detail-oriented, highly organized, and capable of managing multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a goal- and deadline-oriented team environment.
  • Must be service- and solutions-oriented with strong relationship management and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong analytical skills, including ability to gather and analyze a variety of information and develop appropriate recommendations for action.
  • Ability to exercise good judgment and work with minimum of instruction and supervision when necessary.
  • Ability to maintain high standards of confidentiality and professional integrity.
  • Competency in word processing, spreadsheet, and presentation software (MS Office or Google Workspace) required.

Desired Qualifications

  • Familiarity with Raiser’s Edge, Engaging Networks, Mobile Commons, Salesforce Marketing Cloud or other fundraising and SMS platforms, CRMs, or databases preferred.
  • Familiarity with BlueConic, Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud or other CDPs.
  • Familiarity with Monday.com or similar project management platforms.
  • Candidates with experience working for or with external consultants preferred.
  • Ability to relate to people of diverse backgrounds, training, and experience.
  • Possess a growth mindset and high emotional intelligence.

Supervision

No direct reports


Salary Information

The National Geographic Society offers a competitive and holistic total rewards package. Our compensation structure and transparent pay philosophy are based on industry-specific market data for similar-sized nonprofit organizations.

The salary range for this position accounts for a wide range of factors including but not limited to organizational need; specific skill sets; experience and training; certifications; and more. At the National Geographic Society, individuals are typically hired at or near the starting point of the salary range for their role, and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

The salary range for this position is $106,400.00 - $112,000.00.

In addition, the National Geographic Society offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits package that includes, but is not limited to, medical, dental, and vision insurance; engaging and comprehensive wellness program; 401(k) retirement savings plan with matching contributions after 6 months of employment; flexible paid time off benefits with up to 22 days of paid annual leave per calendar year (15 days for new hires in their first year, prorated based on the number of pay periods remaining in the year) and 10 days of sick leave; 12 paid holidays and a paid winter break between December 25 and 31 (May not apply to all roles that are required to work during high volume seasons or essential workers. Please check with the hiring manager for confirmation.); paid parental leave, adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, fertility benefits; learning and development opportunities; Lifestyle Spending Account; pet adoption assistance and insurance; pre-tax transportation benefits with a generous employer subsidy; employer-paid life insurance and disability benefit; and a variety of National Geographic discounts and perks.

Job Designation

Remote - Our Remote designation includes staff who must work in another location in the U.S. or abroad, such as our regional leads for our Education and International teams or regional fundraisers in Advancement. Staff may also be designated as Remote by their supervisors (with approval by the Senior Team lead) because of their job duties, and are afforded this status when it is beneficial to NGS, their respective team, and the employee.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based.

What this opportunity involves

We’re looking for US-based, actively practicing physicians (MD/DO) to evaluate clinical EHR vignettes for a medical AI evaluation program. General and internal medicine are our main focus. While each project involves unique tasks, contributors may:

  • Evaluate clinical EHR vignettes paired with a question, a proposed answer, and a distractor “trap” answer across diagnosis and treatment tasks, spanning cardiovascular, nervous, hematologic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, musculoskeletal, and integumentary systems;
  • Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;
  • Check whether the reasoning chain reaches the answer from vignette facts alone, correct reasoning traces, and write short rationales;
  • Work within three independent blind reads, followed by physician adjudication. Real clinical complexity only. You’re improving the AI tools you’ll eventually use yourself.

If you’re a practicing physician ready to take on this challenging and engaging project, join us!

What we look for

This opportunity is a good fit for US-based physicians open to part-time, non-permanent projects. Ideally, contributors will have:

  • Medical degree (MD or DO) and an active, unrestricted US medical license (verified with the issuing medical board);
  • Board certification or completed residency training, with recent direct patient care (attending-level preferred);
  • Broad, multi-system diagnostic and treatment experience (internal, family, emergency, or hospital medicine);
  • Strong clinical reasoning: differential diagnosis, next-step management, and application of evidence-based guidelines;
  • Prior experience in medical AI evaluation, clinical content or exam-question review, or medical annotation/QA (a plus);
  • Strong written English (C1+).

This opportunity is not fit to medical students, unlicensed medical graduates, non-physician clinicians (NPs, PAs, nurses, pharmacists), or non-clinical healthcare titles.

Project time expectations

For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10-20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active. Tasks must be submitted by the deadline and meet the listed acceptance criteria to be accepted.

Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks — up to the equivalent of $70/hr. Because payment is per approved task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate.

Bilingual Medical Patient Services Coordinator

Location: Remote - Peru
Employment Type: Full-Time Independent Contractor
Number of Openings:10 Positions
Industry: Healthcare Services / Medical Administration
Compensation:$1,280 USD per month
Experience: 1+ Year Supporting U.S. Healthcare Accounts
Languages: Advanced English (C1/C2) and Fluent Spanish
Schedule: Full-Time | U.S. Business Hours
Start Date: As Soon As Possible

About the Company

Our client is a growing U.S.-based healthcare support organization that provides remote administrative and patient service solutions to medical practices across the United States.

The company works with healthcare providers to improve patient communication, streamline appointment management, and reduce the administrative workload of medical teams.

Through its remote workforce, the organization supports essential healthcare operations, including patient scheduling, insurance verification, electronic medical records, and front-office coordination.

The team is focused on delivering reliable administrative assistance that helps medical practices operate efficiently while maintaining a positive patient experience.

About the Role

We are seeking Bilingual Medical Patient Services Coordinators to provide remote front-desk and patient communication support to U.S.-based medical practices.

You will be responsible for assisting patients through phone calls, emails, and messages, coordinating appointments, confirming insurance eligibility, and maintaining accurate patient information.

As an important point of contact between patients and healthcare providers, you will help ensure that daily administrative activities run smoothly and that patients receive professional, friendly, and timely assistance.

This opportunity is ideal for someone with previous experience supporting U.S. healthcare operations who enjoys patient interaction, communicates confidently in English and Spanish, and can manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.

What You'll Do

Patient Communication & Front Desk Services

  • Respond to incoming patient calls, emails, and electronic messages.

  • Make outbound calls for appointment confirmations, follow-ups, and other administrative requests.

  • Assist patients with routine questions and direct inquiries to the appropriate healthcare team members.

  • Communicate professionally with physicians, medical staff, and patients.

  • Deliver friendly, empathetic, and efficient customer service.

  • Protect confidential patient information during all interactions.

Appointment Scheduling & Patient Coordination

  • Schedule, confirm, cancel, and reschedule medical appointments.

  • Maintain accurate provider calendars and appointment details.

  • Coordinate scheduling updates between patients and medical teams.

  • Assist patients with appointment-related questions and follow-up communication.

  • Help ensure scheduling processes remain organized and efficient.

Insurance & Patient Records Administration

  • Verify patient insurance eligibility and benefit information.

  • Review and update patient demographic information.

  • Maintain accurate records within Electronic Medical Record (EMR) and Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems.

  • Identify missing or outdated patient information and coordinate necessary updates.

  • Support accurate documentation and administrative recordkeeping.

Daily Medical Office Support

  • Update reports, databases, and administrative files.

  • Assist with routine documentation and data entry.

  • Support additional administrative tasks and special projects as needed.

  • Coordinate with healthcare team members to resolve outstanding administrative requests.

  • Maintain organized workflows and ensure assigned responsibilities are completed on time.

Qualifications

Required

  • At least 1 year of experience supporting U.S. healthcare accounts through a medical practice, BPO, CPO, or freelance healthcare environment.

  • Advanced English proficiency (C1/C2) and fluent Spanish, both written and spoken.

  • Clear, professional spoken English with a neutral or minimal accent.

  • Experience working with EMR/EHR systems.

  • Previous experience verifying patient insurance eligibility and benefits.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Google Workspace.

  • Strong customer service and patient communication skills.

  • Excellent organization, multitasking, and time-management abilities.

  • Ability to maintain accurate documentation and patient information.

  • Comfortable communicating directly with patients in a busy healthcare environment.

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively with remote teams.

  • Availability during U.S. business hours.

Preferred

  • Degree or relevant coursework in an Allied Health field.

  • Experience supporting U.S.-based physicians or medical practices.

  • Previous experience with patient scheduling and appointment management.

  • Familiarity with HIPAA regulations and patient confidentiality requirements.

  • Experience providing remote administrative or front-desk support in healthcare.

What Makes a Strong Candidate?

We are particularly interested in professionals who demonstrate:

  • Patient-focused communication: You interact with patients professionally, patiently, and empathetically.

  • Strong phone skills: You communicate clearly and confidently in English and Spanish.

  • Organization: You manage appointments, records, and administrative requests accurately.

  • Attention to detail: You understand the importance of correct patient information and insurance documentation.

  • Multitasking: You can balance calls, scheduling, and administrative responsibilities.

  • Reliability: You follow through on pending requests and complete tasks on time.

  • Adaptability: You can work effectively in a fast-paced, remote healthcare environment.

How Success Is Measured

  • Patients receive timely, courteous, and professional assistance.

  • Inbound and outbound communications are handled efficiently.

  • Appointment calendars remain accurate and organized.

  • Insurance eligibility and patient demographic information are verified correctly.

  • EMR/EHR records are maintained accurately.

  • Administrative tasks are completed within expected timelines.

  • Medical teams receive consistent and dependable front-office support.

  • Patient interactions contribute to a positive healthcare experience.

Why Join Us?

  • 100% remote opportunity supporting medical practices in the United States.

  • Join a growing organization specializing in healthcare support services.

  • Develop experience in U.S. medical front-office operations.

  • Work directly with patient scheduling, insurance verification, and EMR/EHR systems.

  • Collaborate with healthcare professionals across different medical specialties.

  • Gain valuable experience in patient services and healthcare administration.

Important Notes

  • Advanced English (C1/C2) and fluent Spanish are mandatory.

  • Candidates must have at least 1 year of experience supporting U.S. healthcare accounts.

  • Experience with EMR/EHR systems and insurance eligibility verification is required.

  • Clear and professional spoken English with a neutral or minimal accent is expected.

This is a fully remote position.

Leadership

Market & Competitive Intelligence

jobs.excerpt: We're looking for a Senior AI Developer to design, build and run production-grade agentic AI systems on AWS and Azure.
jobs.description:
We're looking for a Senior AI Developer to design, build and run production-grade agentic AI systems on AWS and Azure. You'll turn business problems into reliable multi-step agent workflows that use LLMs, tools and enterprise data. You'll own solutions from architecture and prototyping through deployment, evaluation and monitoring, and you'll set engineering standards for how we build with AI.

What you will do

  • Design and build agentic AI systems: single and multi-agent workflows with planning, tool use, memory and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • Develop LLM applications on AWS (Amazon Bedrock, Bedrock Agents/AgentCore) and Azure (Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry / Azure AI Foundry), and recommend the right platform and model for each use case.
  • Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, including data ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector search and grounding over enterprise data.
  • Integrate agents with internal systems, APIs and SaaS tools, using standards such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and function/tool calling.
  • Implement evaluation frameworks for quality, accuracy, safety and cost, including regression tests, LLM-as-judge methods and human review.
  • Add guardrails and responsible-AI controls: prompt-injection defences, content filtering, PII handling, access control and audit logging.
  • Containerise and deploy services with CI/CD and infrastructure as code, and add observability (tracing, logging, latency and token-cost monitoring).
  • Optimise performance, reliability and cost across models, prompts and infrastructure.
  • Mentor engineers, run design and code reviews, and document architectures and decisions.
  • Work with product owners, data teams, security and architecture to take AI use cases from idea to production.

Requirements

What you need to be successful

Must have

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, with 2+ years building LLM or GenAI applications in production.
  • Strong Python skills, plus experience building and operating APIs and services.
  • Hands-on experience building agentic systems with a modern framework (for example LangGraph, LangChain, Microsoft Agent Framework / Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, Strands Agents or CrewAI).
  • Production experience on at least one of AWS or Azure AI services, and working knowledge of the other.
  • Practical RAG experience with vector databases or search services (for example OpenSearch, Azure AI Search, pgvector or Pinecone).
  • Experience with cloud fundamentals: containers (Docker, Kubernetes or serverless), networking and identity (IAM / Entra ID), and secrets management.
  • Experience with CI/CD, Git and infrastructure as code (Terraform, Bicep or CloudFormation).
  • Understanding of LLM evaluation, prompt engineering, and safety and security risks specific to AI systems.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to explain trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with MCP servers, multi-agent protocols (for example A2A), or agent orchestration at scale.
  • Fine-tuning or model customization, and experience with open-source models.
  • Background in a regulated sector such as banking, healthcare or government.
  • Cloud certifications (for example AWS Certified AI Practitioner or Solutions Architect, Azure AI-102 or AZ-204, AZ-400).
  • Experience with data engineering (Spark, Databricks, Fabric or Glue) and data governance.
  • Experience mentoring or leading small teams.

About the Company

Armada is the hyperscaler for the edge, delivering modular AI infrastructure from first deployment to AI factory with speed, scale and sovereignty. Named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and to the CNBC Disruptor 50, Armada’s solutions are deployed in over 60 countries globally for organizations ranging from energy to defense.

With nearly $500 million in funding to date, Armada is backed by leading investors including Founders Fund, Lux, BlackRock and Microsoft (M12), alongside strategic partnerships with Microsoft, Dell, Palantir, NVIDIA, SpaceX, and Skydio. We are building the infrastructure layer for sovereign and edge AI - rugged, deployable compute for customers that cannot rely on centralized cloud.

Working at Armada means taking ownership, driving autonomy, and delivering impact. You’ll tackle challenges that haven’t been solved before and help build something transformative from the ground up. What you do here will not only define your career but help further Armada’s mission to bridge the digital divide for customers around the world.

About the Role

We’re seeking a hands-on, detail-oriented Sales Compensation Analyst Contractor to run the execution side of Armada’s global sales compensation program. This role sits within the Revenue Operations organization, reports to the Director of Sales Operations, and partners with Sales, Customer Success, Finance, and Legal to make sure plans are built correctly, payouts run on time, and reps get clean answers.

The Sales Compensation Analyst will own the monthly commission close in CaptivateIQ, maintain the payee roster and plan assignments, build and test plans for approved designs, and produce the plan documents, quota letters, and cost models that support each rollout. Armada’s compensation program is scaling quickly across new lines of business and geographies, so this is a build-and-run role: you will stabilize a young system, document it, and hand it over clean.

Location. This role is remote-based on the continental US.

Engagement.This is a part-time contract engagement of approximately 190–250 total hours from October 2026 through January 2027, averaging 12–16 hours per week but a higher level of activity in late October and across January. Scope concentrates around the monthly close calendar, two plan rollouts, and FY28 plan build preparation, with optionality for an extended contract or full-time role for strong performance.

What You'll Do (Key Responsibilities)

  • Own the monthly commission close in CaptivateIQ: validate inputs, calculate payouts, investigate variances, and package results for Finance approval on a fixed calendar
  • Maintain the payee roster, plan assignments, hierarchies, and quota records in CaptivateIQ as people, territories, and plans change
  • Build, configure, and test compensation plans in CaptivateIQ for approved designs spanning new and evolving roles and business units
  • Produce quota letters and compensation agreements from approved templates; manage DocuSign routing, tracking, and filing through to full execution
  • Build cost models, payout scenarios, and rep-level summaries from approved plan designs to support leadership review

jobs.excerpt: For People is improving government digital services for the disadvantaged population.
jobs.description:
For People is improving government digital services for the disadvantaged population. We work directly with government agencies to modernize software, systems, and platforms so that they better serve people.

Your Impact

Every month, hundreds of thousands of people go looking for facts about Medicare and Medicaid. They are researchers, reporters, policy staff, and health care providers. When the data is hard to find, a file is too large to post, or a column quietly changes its name between releases, their work slows down or goes wrong.

This project supports the website where the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) publishes that data for the public. It hosts a large catalog of datasets, lookup tools, and dashboards from across the agency, available for download, as interactive tools, and via a public API. As Program Manager, you will lead the team that builds and runs it. This is a hands-on role. You’ll facilitate partner meetings, support the team when they are blocked, and get into project details as needed to report clearly on the team’s progress. You’ll work elbow-to-elbow with the project’s technical and product leadership. You will learn about the work enough to identify and help mitigate delivery risks and hold the team accountable for what we promise to government partners.

This position is a full-time position contingent on For People being awarded a federal contract. If awarded, this position’s expected start date is February 2027.

Our Culture

For People is a team of humans. We place a significant amount of emphasis on positive work-life balance, setting healthy expectations, and making sure our loved ones are taken care of first. That means picking a child up from school during the day or going for a mid-day walk is okay!

This position is 100% remote. Our entire team is remote across the United States, from the West Coast to the East Coast. There will never be a return-to-office, as we have none! Occasional travel to CMS headquarters in Baltimore, MD (2-3 times per year) is required. These trips are infrequent and scheduled well in advance.

This full-time position's published base salary range is between $100,000 and $160,000 annually. This band ranges across both the Program Manager and Senior Program Manager pay band, which will be determined based on relevant experience. All positions include generous benefits (e.g., For People pays 100% of Gold-tier employee health insurance premiums) and annual company profit sharing.

Your Opportunities

On this project, you will be the delivery lead on a cross-functional team of about 15 people spanning engineering, design, user research, and support functions. The team may expand to up to 25 members in the future. As the Program Manager, you will:

  • Build a collaborative and trusting team culture across all disciplines in the program
  • Run agile practices including sprints, planning cycles, demos, and retrospectives, all of which include CMS stakeholders
  • Coordinate with CMS offices that publish data on the public portal; share progress transparently and build positive working relationships with partner contracting teams
  • Proactively identify and mitigate risks to project delivery
  • Keep the program in line with contract, security, and accessibility requirements, including Section 508 and the site's Authority to Operate (ATO)
  • Report status and outcomes to CMS and For People leadership, using live dashboards wherever possible and finding efficiency gains through automation
  • Lead the handoff from the current contractor in your first few months so users see no disruption

You Bring

  • A humble and caring attitude aligning with For People’s values: passion, fun, curiosity, sustainability, humility, and respect
  • 8+ years of relevant experience in program or project management, including managing government contracts
  • Degree in management, public administration, information technology, or a related field
  • Experience with open data projects
  • Experience managing cross-functional teams, with the ability to lead teams of 15 to 25 people as the contract grows
  • Deep knowledge of agile product management principles
  • Familiarity with collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, Slack, and GitHub
  • Ability to oversee all aspects of task order management including reporting, sprint planning, and project planning
  • Experience facilitating stakeholder engagement across multiple government agency offices and data owners

It Would Be Great If You Also Have

  • Experience working directly with CMS programs or data
  • Experience with public websites built on Drupal
  • Experience leading a contract transition from an incumbent team

Some Fine Print

You will be working on a United States government platform, and they have a few basic requirements for contractors like ourselves. All work must be physically performed within the United States at all times. In addition, you must be a United States citizen and be able to pass a government-performed public trust background check.

For People is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, and/or veteran status.

jobs.excerpt: About Modular SolutionsFounded in 2015, Modular Solutions delivers enterprise-grade technology to the insurance industry.
jobs.description:
About Modular Solutions

Founded in 2015, Modular Solutions delivers enterprise-grade technology to the insurance industry. Our configurable platform helps insurers, mutuals, MGAs, and brokers manage core operations through a single system designed for flexibility, long-term growth, and complex regulated environments.

Position Summary

Modular Solutions is seeking a Director of Data & Analytics to own the architecture and governance of our data and analytics platform and how our data is turned into decisions, so that the data we collect becomes reporting and answers that clients and teams can trust as we continue to grow our platform, client base, and internal capabilities.

Reporting to the CTO, this role leads the Data function, including data engineering, data science, business intelligence, analytics, and migration, and owns the architecture of the data and analytics platform that connects them. While the data and analytics platform is the primary focus, the role also contributes to and collaborates on the data architecture and design of our core application alongside our Product and Development teams.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on leader who sets direction and stays close to the work: designing the analytics data architecture, data models, and semantic layer alongside engineers rather than managing from a distance. You should bring deep experience in data architecture, data modelling, BI and analytics, and data governance, with a working knowledge of data migration and AI-enabled workflows, along with the ability to lead people, prioritize work, and translate complex technical concepts into clear business outcomes.

This role is well suited for someone who can build structure, develop teams, improve processes, and help Modular responsibly adopt data and AI practices that create real value for clients, employees, and the platform.

Key Responsibilities

  • Set the data strategy and long-term roadmap for the Data function, including platforms, vendors, budget, and cost, and build a high-performing team across data engineering, BI and analytics, and data migration.
  • Own the data and analytics platform architecture: the target-state design for how data flows out of our application into ingestion and pipelines, the data warehouse and data marts, the semantic layer, and the BI and AI tools that consume them, supported by reference architectures and documented architecture decisions.
  • Define and maintain the analytics data model for insurance data, including policy, billing, claims, bordereaux, brokers, and coverage, aligned with the application's data model, so that migration, reporting, and analytics map to it consistently.
  • Collaborate with Product and Development on the data architecture and design of our core application: bring a data perspective to schema and data model design, assess the downstream impact of changes, favour incremental improvements over large-scale redesign, and establish data contracts so that application changes do not break reporting, integrations, or client deliverables.
  • Own metric governance: a single set of business definitions and KPIs with clear owners, implemented once in the semantic layer and consumed consistently by BI, client reporting, and AI.
  • Design how clients access their reporting and analytics data, including governed data sharing and extracts, partnering with product engineering where access runs through application APIs, with appropriate tenant isolation, security, and performance.
  • Set standards for data quality, governance, privacy, security, and data residency, including PII classification, retention, lineage, and access control, in support of our security and compliance programs.
  • Establish a data quality and validation framework, including automated reconciliation, testing, and certification of trusted datasets and AI-generated outputs, so that our teams and clients can trust results at scale.
  • Define the reporting operating model for standard and client-specific reporting, including intake and prioritization, move clients toward governed self-service analytics, and deliver executive-level insights and advanced analytics, such as forecasting, where they create clear business value.
  • Build data migration and onboarding into a repeatable capability, with a reusable conversion framework, reconciliation, and post-migration validation, led by a dedicated migration lead.
  • Build AI-ready data foundations so that AI features call governed data and semantic models rather than calculating on their own, lead AI adoption within the Data team, and help define the product direction for self-service and AI-assisted analytics.
  • Partner with Product, Development, Implementation, Operations, and leadership to align priorities, and communicate progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly to executives.
  • Perform other duties as required to support the Data function.

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in data architecture, data engineering, business intelligence, analytics, or a related data field, including designing data platforms or data models at an organizational level.
  • 3+ years of experience leading, mentoring, or managing technical teams, while remaining hands-on in the work.
  • Proven experience designing enterprise data architecture, including data models, data warehouses and marts, ETL/ELT pipelines, semantic models, and the integration between operational systems and analytics platforms, with a track record of collaborating with application engineering teams on data design and improving existing systems incrementally.
  • Hands-on experience building and governing business definitions, metrics, or semantic models, and working directly with engineers to implement them.
  • Strong grounding in data governance, data quality, privacy, and security, including access control, PII handling, lineage, and validation of data and reporting outputs.
  • Experience leading data migration, data conversion, or reconciliation initiatives.
  • Strong technical knowledge of SQL, relational databases, and cloud data platforms, with experience in tools such as Snowflake, PostgreSQL, Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, Azure, and Python, or similar technologies. Familiarity with C# or TypeScript is an asset.
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools in day-to-day work, and the ability to encourage and support their use across a team, with sound judgment on accuracy, privacy, and security.
  • Experience designing KPI frameworks and delivering executive-level reporting, with strong data visualization and storytelling skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate business needs into technical direction and technical concepts into clear business language, and to set standards and repeatable operating models across technical and non-technical teams.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage ambiguity, competing priorities, and cross-functional dependencies.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Background in the insurance, InsurTech, SaaS, financial services, or other complex regulated environments.
  • Familiarity with insurance data, including policy, billing, claims, broker, customer, coverage, risk, transaction, or reporting data.
  • Previous involvement in AI adoption, AI enablement, or AI transformation initiatives within a software, data, or product organization.
  • Hands-on exposure to AI-powered internal tools, workflow automation, document analysis, reporting automation, data validation, or agentic systems.
  • Experience with multi-tenant SaaS data architectures, client data sharing, or data residency requirements.
  • Proven ability to partner with Product, Development, Implementation, and executive leadership teams to align data and AI initiatives with business priorities.
  • Familiarity with Agile delivery tools and practices, including Azure DevOps, Jira, Scrum, Kanban, or similar methodologies.
  • Ability to scale teams, hire technical talent, and support career growth for data and AI professionals.

What Success Looks Like in Your First Year

  • A documented target-state analytics data architecture and data model, with a roadmap agreed with business and engineering leadership.
  • A governed semantic layer in production for our released data marts, serving as the single source of business definitions for reporting and AI.
  • Automated validation in place for key client reporting, including bordereaux, replacing manual checking.
  • A repeatable data migration framework, with a dedicated migration lead in place.
  • A clear reporting operating model and a plan for client self-service analytics.

Our Technology Stack and Architecture:

Our core platform uses C#/.NET, Entity Framework, PostgreSQL, React, TypeScript, and Azure, with Snowflake as our data warehouse. This role partners with product engineering teams on system logic, database structures, APIs, and platform requirements related to data architecture, migration, BI, the semantic layer, data quality, and automation workflows.

Why Join Modular Solutions?

We are building a long-term platform in a complex industry where customers depend on accurate data every day. You will shape how Modular architects its data and turns it into trusted reporting and answers for clients: designing the analytics data architecture, defining what the numbers mean, and building the semantic layer alongside a strong engineering team, while making migration and BI work cleaner, faster, and more AI-enabled as we grow. We value autonomy, accountability, strong technical judgment, and people who take pride in building production-grade systems the right way.

What We Offer

  • Be part of a growing company building a modern, enterprise-grade platform for the insurance industry.
  • Work alongside experienced insurance and technology professionals in a collaborative environment.
  • Flexible remote work environment, with a preference for Alberta-based team members, and periodic in-person planning sessions and team events.
  • Extended health, dental, and vision benefits.
  • Access to an Employee and Family Assistance Program.
  • Annual professional development allowance.
  • Additional paid time off beyond standard statutory holidays and vacation.
  • Recognition for meaningful contributions and career milestones.
  • Share Appreciation Rights program so you participate in the company’s long-term success.

To Apply:

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience and what excites you about this opportunity. We thank all applicants for their interest; only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.description:
IT Systems Administrator

Position Overview

This role is designed for someone with solid IT fundamentals who will provide essential technical support across our technology ecosystem. The position offers learning opportunities in Productivity Platforms, Identity, Security and Device Management, while handling day-to-day operational responsibilities that keep our teams productive.

Core Remit of Responsibilities

1. Helpdesk Support

Primary Accountability: Act as the first point of contact for technical issues and requests

Day-to-day activities:

  • Respond to and triage incoming support tickets and requests via Slack or our ticketing system.

  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues with SaaS systems and end user devices (Windows / macOS / Linux)

  • Support video conferencing endpoints and meeting room technology (Zoom, MS Teams and Google Meet.)

  • Escalate complex issues to senior team members with appropriate context and initial diagnostics

  • Maintain accurate documentation of issues, resolutions, and user interactions

  • Meet agreed service level agreements (SLAs) for response and resolution times

  • Monitoring Infrastructure

2. Productivity Suite Administration

Primary Accountability: Manage and support Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 environments

Day-to-day activities:

  • Create, modify, and delete user accounts in Google Workspace and Microsoft 365

  • Manage user licenses and entitlements across both platforms

  • Configure email accounts, distribution lists, and shared mailboxes

  • Set up and manage Google Drive permissions

  • Troubleshoot email delivery issues, calendar conflicts, and sharing problems

  • Support Microsoft Teams and Google Meet configuration and access

  • Implement security policies such as MFA enforcement and password policies

  • Generate basic reports on usage and license allocation

3. Onboarding and Offboarding

Primary Accountability: Ensure smooth technology transitions for joiners and leavers

Day-to-day activities:

  • Coordinate with HR to receive advance notice of new starters and departures

  • Prepare laptops and devices for new employees where required

  • Create all necessary user accounts and assign appropriate access permissions

  • Conduct welcome sessions to set up new employees with their technology

  • Create and maintain onboarding checklists and documentation

  • Execute offboarding procedures including account deactivation, data backup/transfer, and device retrieval

  • Ensure security protocols are followed during offboarding (credential removal, access revocation)

  • Maintain asset inventory records for all issued equipment

4. Mobile Device Management (MDM)

Primary Accountability: Manage and secure company end-user devices

Day-to-day activities:

  • Ensure new devices are enrolled into MDM platform and identities are linked

  • Deploy and manage configuration and application profiles for security and compliance

  • Ensure deployment of software updates and security patches to managed devices

  • Remotely troubleshoot device issues and perform remote wipes when necessary

  • Monitor compliance dashboards and address non-compliant devices

  • Maintain documentation of MDM policies and device inventories

5. Infrastructure Support (Foundational Level)

Primary Accountability: Develop working knowledge of infrastructure while providing basic support

Day-to-day activities:

  • Monitor server health and availability alerts under guidance

  • Assist with routine server maintenance tasks (updates, backups verification)

  • Support basic networking tasks such as switch port configurations and Wi-Fi troubleshooting

  • Learn and assist with storage management

  • Shadow senior team members during firewall rule changes and network configurations

  • Document infrastructure procedures and maintain network diagrams

  • Participate in infrastructure projects to build practical experience

Required Skills & Competencies

Technical Skills - Essential

Helpdesk & Support:

  • 5+ years experience in a helpdesk or technical support role

  • Strong troubleshooting methodology and logical problem-solving approach

  • Experience supporting Windows 10/11 and macOS operating systems

  • Familiarity with common business applications and SaaS platforms

  • Understanding of basic networking concepts (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP)

Productivity Platforms:

  • Hands-on experience administering Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 (ideally both)

  • Understanding of cloud identity management and user provisioning

  • Experience with file sharing and collaboration tools

Device Management:

  • Experience managing MDM platforms

  • Knowledge of security policies and device compliance requirements

  • EDR - NG anti-virus and firewall administration (Crowdstrike)

Infrastructure (Foundational):

  • Basic understanding of server operating systems (Linux)

  • Awareness of networking fundamentals (IP addressing, vlans, firewall rules )

  • Familiarity with virtualization concepts

  • Understanding of backup and disaster recovery principles

Technical Skills - Desirable

  • CompTIA A+, Network+, or similar certifications

  • Microsoft 365 Certified: Fundamentals or Associate level

  • Google Workspace Administrator certification

  • Experience with scripting (PowerShell, Bash) for basic automation

  • Experience with video conferencing platforms and endpoints (Zoom, Teams, G-Meet)

Soft Skills & Attributes - Essential

  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical users with patience and clarity

  • Customer Service Orientation: Genuine desire to help others and provide outstanding user experience

  • Learning Agility: Enthusiasm for learning new technologies and adapting to change; proactive about skill development

  • Time Management: Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and manage workload effectively

  • Attention to Detail: Thoroughness in documentation and following procedures

  • Team Collaboration: Works well within a team environment and willing to support colleagues

  • Problem-Solving: Analytical mindset with persistence in resolving technical challenges

  • Professional Maturity: Reliable, punctual, and maintains confidentiality with sensitive information
